TI Exploring students' well-being: insights from Indonesian fast-track
   postgraduate program
SO PSIKHOLOGICHESKAYA NAUKA I OBRAZOVANIE-PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCE AND
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE well-being; postgraduate students' challenges; Indonesia; fasttrack
   program
AB Context and relevance. Pursuing a postgraduate degree in a fast-track program presents significant challenges to students' well-being. Objective. This study aims to explore the well-being of Indonesian postgraduate students in fast-track programs, focusing on their psychological challenges, coping strategies, and the role of coping self-efficacy (CSE) in predicting well-being. Methods and materials. The mixed-methods approach combines quantitative data from an e-survey with qualitative data from focus group discussions. The study involved 180 PMDSU awardees who completed the questionnaire, while 24 participants were selected for focus group discussions. The participants, aged 21-32 (M = 25,28; SD = 1,94; 42,2% of male and 57,8% of female participants), were from various Indonesian universities. Results. The results integrate quantitative findings with qualitative insights into challenges, support systems, and coping strategies among fast-track scholarship awardees. The multiple regression analyses revealed that obtaining social support coping (GS) and stopping unpleasant emotional and thought coping (SE) were significant predictors of various aspects of well-being. Specifically, GS strongly predicted life satisfaction (beta = 0,430; p < 0,001) and positive affect (beta = 0,344; p < 0,001), and was negatively associated with negative affect (beta = -0,244; p = 0,007). SE significantly enhanced positive affect (beta = 0,468; p < 0,001), reduced negative affect (beta = -0,562; p < 0,001), and increased balance affect (beta = 0,568; p < 0,001). Sex significantly predicted negative affect (beta = 0,254; p < 0,001) and balance affect (beta = -0,182, p = 0,001), with females reporting higher negative affect and lower balance affect. No significant effect was found for satisfaction with life or positive affect. Conclusions. The study concludes that awardees face diverse challenges and perceive their coping strategies as effective in overcoming difficulties, achieving academic success, and maintaining well-being. The findings highlight the critical role of emotional regulation and seeking social support as coping strategies in maintaining well-being.

   developing emotional intelligence and existential competence among
   Indonesian university students

AB This study examines the relationship between high school background (general, vocational, and Islamic schools) and daily reflective practices in predicting emotional intelligence (EI) and existential competence (EC) among Indonesian university students. TI Constructivist or instrumentalist? Exploring how pre-service teachers'
   beliefs shape the integration of mathematical values and SDGs
SO PSIKHOLOGICHESKAYA NAUKA I OBRAZOVANIE-PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCE AND
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE mathematical beliefs; pre-service teachers; teaching materials;
   Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs); value
ID STUDENTS
AB Context and relevance. As global challenges intensify, mathematics education faces growing demands to cultivate both abstract reasoning and value orientations aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Pre-service teachers' epistemological beliefs play a critical role in shaping how these elements are incorporated into instructional materials. Objective. This study examines how Indonesian pre-service mathematics teachers' belief orientations - constructivist, Platonist, or instrumentalist - influence their integration of mathematical values (usefulness, creativity, transformation) and SDG themes in teaching resources. Methods and materials. A qualitative design engaged 37 final-year pre-service teachers (15 male, 22 female; aged 20-24) from an Indonesian state university. Data from written reflections and semi-structured interviews were analyzed through theory-driven descriptive coding, with rigor ensured via triangulation, member checking, and audit trails. Results. Analysis revealed distinct pedagogical patterns: constructivistoriented teachers developed materials emphasizing creativity and contextual SDG integration, while Platonist approaches prioritized conceptual rigor and instrumentalist designs focused on procedural applications - both showing comparatively limited depth in value integration. Conclusions. The findings demonstrate how epistemological beliefs shape SDG implementation, suggesting teacher education programs would benefit from systematically addressing belief systems to prepare educators for creating mathematics instruction that balances conceptual mastery, creative reasoning, and global citizenship.

TI The moderating role of innovative work behavior in enhancing teacher
   performance
SO PSIKHOLOGICHESKAYA NAUKA I OBRAZOVANIE-PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCE AND
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE innovative work behavior; participation; quality of learning; teacher
   performance; work motivation
AB Teacher performancein addition to reflecting teacher professionalism, also greatly determines the future of students. To support teacher performance, at least three components are needed to make schools a learning organization. They are transformative leadership, an inclusive work environment, and a progressive learning process, which are firmly embedded in teacher motivation, making teaching not just a routine but a mobilization of all abilities in the form of innovative work behavior to participate in organizing quality learning. The study examines the moderating effect of innovative work behavior on the relationship between work motivation and participation, and its influence on teacher performance. It is hypothesized that work motivation, participation, and innovative work behavior positively affect teacher performance, and that innovative work behavior moderates the relationship between motivation and participation. The study employs a quantitative approach with an ex post facto design. Data were collected from 317 junior high school teachers in Temanggung Regency, Indonesia, through proportional random sampling techniques. The Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) technique was applied to analyze the relationship between variables. The results of the study indicate that transformative principal leadership has been proven to strengthen work motivation, encourage participation, and increase teachers' innovative work behavior. Strengthening work motivation can be achieved by improving teacher morale, acknowledging teacher performance, creating a conducive work environment, and presenting awards - both financial and non-financial - to teachers who excel and are dedicated to student success and school progress. Increasing participation can be achieved by involving teachers in formulating school policies, developing school curricula and activities, fostering an inclusive and collaborative culture, and providing opportunities for teachers to take the initiative. Coaching and promoting innovative work behavior can be achieved by creating an adaptive and creative learning environment that encourages a progressive learning process, fostering various innovations and new ideas in learning.

TI Problem-solving as a bridge: mediating the relationship between
   creativity and student burnout
SO PSIKHOLOGICHESKAYA NAUKA I OBRAZOVANIE-PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCE AND
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE academic performance; burnout; coping; creativity; problem-solving;
   undergraduate students
ID UNIVERSITY-STUDENTS; ACADEMIC BURNOUT; METAANALYSIS; STRESS
AB Context and relevance. Burnout is a common concern among university students. While cognitive-behavioral coping strategies such as creativity and problem-solving may shape how students manage academic stress, limited research has examined their roles in relation to student burnout. Objective. This study aimed to investigate the relationships among creativity, problem-solving, and burnout in a sample of Iranian undergraduate students. Hypothesis. It was hypothesized that higher levels of creativity and problem-solving would be associated with lower levels of student burnout. Methods and materials. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 193 undergraduate students (73,1% female, 26,9% male) aged 18-25 years (M = 21,2, SD = 1,5) from a university in southern Iran. Participants completed the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Student Survey (MBI-SS), the Abedi-Schumacher Creativity Test, and the Social Problem-Solving Inventory (SPSI). Creativity and problem-solving were both negatively correlated with student burnout. However, in the regression analysis, problem-solving demonstrated the strongest unique association with burnout, whereas creativity was no longer independently associated with burnout. Exploratory mediation analysis further suggested that problem-solving may mediate the association between creativity and burnout. Conclusions. Problem-solving appears to be strongly associated with lower levels of student burnout, and creativity may contribute indirectly through its relationship with problem-solving. These findings may inform the development of academic support strategies aimed at enhancing students' coping resources. Further research is needed to explore these associations over time.

TI Understanding the psychological pathway linking parental phubbing to
   academic burnout among Chinese high school students: the role of
   alienation
SO PSIKHOLOGICHESKAYA NAUKA I OBRAZOVANIE-PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCE AND
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE parental phubbing; academic burnout; alienation; high school students
ID SELF-DETERMINATION
AB Context and relevance. Academic burnout has become a major concern among adolescents in exam-oriented educational systems. Parental phubbing, defined as parents' distraction by smartphones during interactions, is increasingly recognized as a potential risk factor for students' psychological and academic adjustment. Objective. This study examined the psychological pathway linking parental phubbing to academic burnout among Chinese high school students, with particular attention to the role of alienation within the framework of Self-Determination Theory. Hypothesis. It was hypothesized that parental phubbing would be positively associated with alienation and academic burnout, that alienation would be positively associated with academic burnout, and that alienation would mediate the association between parental phubbing and academic burnout. Methods and materials. A total of 511 students (M = 17,0; SD = 0,88; 54,4% female) from Shanxi and Heilongjiang provinces completed validated questionnaires assessing parental phubbing, alienation, and academic burnout. Structural equation modeling was performed using SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results. Parental phubbing was positively associated with both alienation and academic burnout. Alienation significantly predicted academic burnout and partially mediated the association between parental phubbing and academic burnout. Gender differences were observed, with female students reporting higher levels of burnout. Conclusions. The findings suggest that alienation represents an important psychological pathway through which parental phubbing may be associated with academic burnout among Chinese high school students. The results highlight the relevance of adolescents' perceived relational disconnection in understanding the academic consequences of digitally distracted parenting.

TI Digital humusities in teacher education in Latin America: historical
   reflections between Brazil and Argentina
SO REVISTA IBERO-AMERICANA DE ESTUDOS EM EDUCACAO
LA English
DT Article
DE digital citizenship; South-South academic cooperation; teacher
   education; humusities; decolonial pedagogies
AB This article proposes a theoretical-epistemological and historical reflection on the intersections between digital citizenship and decolonial teacher education in Latin America, based on a comparative and situated analysis between Brazil and Argentina. TI Evaluating the Teaching Effectiveness of Interactive Virtual Platform
   Based on Artificial Intelligence for Obstetrics and Gynecology Residency
   Training
SO ADVANCES IN MEDICAL EDUCATION AND PRACTICE
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence; obstetrics and gynecology; residency training;
   six core competencies; virtual platform
AB Objective: This study aims to create and validate the teaching effectiveness of an interactive artificial intelligence (AI) virtual platform in the standardized residency training of obstetricians and gynecologists. Methods: This study randomly selected 70 obstetricians and gynecologists undergoing standardized training at the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital affiliated with Zhejiang University School of Medicine. The participants were divided into an experimental group and a control group in a 1:1 ratio. The results of the patient satisfaction survey showed that the evaluation of the experimental group physicians in terms of medical ability, communication ability, and medical ethics was also better than that of the control group (P < 0.05). Conclusion: The addition of AI-based virtual case training to standard teaching-clinic practice in obstetrics and gynecology education is an effective innovative approach. This platform not only enriches teaching resources and enhances the core competencies of resident physicians but also significantly improves teaching satisfaction and patient satisfaction.

TI Associations Between Parenting Stress, Parenting Behaviours and Language
   Abilities in Autistic Preschoolers: A Study with Mothers and Fathers
SO AUTISM & DEVELOPMENTAL LANGUAGE IMPAIRMENTS
LA English
DT Article
DE Autism; preschoolers; language development; parenting; gender
   differences
ID SCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN; SPECTRUM DISORDER; MATERNAL STRESS; FAMILIES;
   ADOLESCENTS; PREDICTORS; CHILDHOOD; HEALTH
AB Background and Aims Research shows that language abilities in autism are highly heterogeneous and that parents play a crucial role in children's development. However, the bidirectional relationships between parenting stress, parenting behaviours and children's language abilities in autism remain under-researched. Furthermore, fathers are often excluded from autism parenting research. This study therefore aimed (1) to compare mothers and fathers with respect to the levels of self-reported parenting stress and behaviours and (2) to examine associations between parenting stress, parenting behaviours and children's language abilities, as well as whether these associations differ between mothers and fathers.Methods This cross-sectional study included 92 autistic children aged 2-6 with their mothers and fathers. Parenting stress and parenting behaviours were measured with self-report questionnaires. Children's receptive and expressive language abilities were measured using a combination of standardised tests, which were chosen depending on the children's age, abilities and community language (i.e., Dutch or French). Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to compare mothers and fathers. Zero-order and partial Spearman correlations were adopted to examine associations among variables, and Fisher's r-to-z transformations compared the strength of associations between maternal and paternal correlations.Results Mothers reported higher scores on parenting stress and several positive parenting behaviours (i.e., positive parenting, supervision, rules, rewarding, stimulating the development and adapting the environment) than fathers. No significant differences were found in the amount of autonomy support, discipline and indulging. In mothers, multiple parenting behaviours (i.e., autonomy support, supervision, discipline and stimulating the development) were significantly correlated with children's language abilities, although these associations weakened when controlling for children's non-verbal cognitive abilities. In fathers, only supervision correlated significantly with children's language abilities. Mothers showed no significant associations between self-reported parenting stress and behaviours. In fathers, however, higher parenting stress was linked to lower positive parenting, rewarding and stimulating the development and to higher discipline and indulging. Paternal stress was also related to lower receptive language abilities, a pattern not observed in mothers.Conclusions More differences than similarities emerged in parenting experiences and practices between mothers and fathers. Mothers reported more parenting stress and positive parenting practices compared to fathers, whereas no differences were found for negative parenting practices. Gender differences also appeared in the associations between parenting stress, parenting behaviours and child's language abilities. More specifically, maternal parenting behaviours were more strongly related to children's language abilities than paternal parenting behaviours. Importantly, these associations weakened after controlling for children's cognition, suggesting a complex interplay between these variables to be further researched. Parenting stress was related to both parenting behaviours and children's language abilities only in fathers, and not in mothers.Implications These findings suggest the importance of including both mothers and fathers in autism parenting research and clinical practice.
   They encourage future longitudinal and intervention studies to further examine the interrelations between parenting stress, parenting behaviours and children's language development, while also considering the role of child characteristics that may influence these associations, in order to inform parent-mediated language interventions.

TI AI-Generated Videos to Improve Content Comprehension in Contrastive
   Grammar and Research Methods
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTER-ASSISTED LANGUAGE LEARNING AND
   TEACHING
LA English
DT Article
DE AI-Generated Videos; English as a Foreign Language; Teacher Education;
   Student Engagement; Reflective Practice; Digital Skills; Content
   Comprehension; Academic Achievement; Universidad Tecnica Particular de
   Loja
ID PERFORMANCE; INTELLIGENCE; ENGAGEMENT; SCIENCE; IMPACT
AB This mixed-methods study examined the effectiveness of AI-generated instructional videos (AIVs) on content comprehension, engagement, and reflective practice. Conducted with 117 undergraduate students in an Ecuadorian English-as-a-foreign-language teacher education program, the study compared AIV-supported instruction with traditional materials in two courses: Contrastive Grammar and Research Methods. Quantitative data from tests, surveys, and reflection scores were complemented by qualitative analysis of student reflections and classroom artifacts. Results showed that students using AIVs outperformed the control group in Contrastive Grammar, while gains in Research Methods were positive but not statistically significant. Students reported high perceived usefulness and moderate to high engagement, despite some challenges in video creation. Moreover, watching AIVs helped students clarify and reinforce content, while creating videos fostered deeper understanding, creativity, and digital skills. Reflection quality strongly correlated with academic achievement in Research Methods but not in Contrastive Grammar.

TI Harmonising Competency-Based Medical and Dental Curricula in Ghana
SO JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND CURRICULAR DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE harmonization; curricula; framework; interviews; leadership;
   mixed-methods; survey
ID EDUCATION
AB Background Competency-based education improves the quantity and quality of healthcare professionals, though many countries are yet to transition from traditional education. This study aimed to identify competencies for medical and dental undergraduates in Ghana, and explore experiences and perceptions of implementing competency-based education in medical and dental undergraduate programmes in Ghana.Methods A two-day consensus workshop was held, alongside semi-structured interviews with medical and dental leadership in Ghana, and an online survey of medical and dental faculty and students. In the workshop, a nominal group technique was used to reach consensus on competencies. Interviews explored perceptions of competency-based education and its implementation with medical and dental leaders. The online survey was distributed across all faculty in medical and dental schools in Ghana and cascaded to students to explore perceptions of competency-based education amongst faculty and student stakeholders. Interview and survey participant characteristics are narratively summarised, with open-ended survey responses and interview transcripts undergoing content and thematic analysis respectively.Results Twenty-six leaders took part in the consensus workshop, with 18 of these interviewed. Completed surveys were received from 70 participants. A ten domain, 63-item competency framework for medical and dental graduates in Ghana was produced. Competency-based education was perceived positively by all stakeholder groups, and reported as the way forward in medical and dental education in Ghana through producing more confident and competent graduates. Challenges were raised, including ensuring stakeholder buy-in, organising regulator and institution communications, and securing physical infrastructure, digital resources and funding. The concept of harmonising curricula was positively received, having been previously attempted by several institutions in Ghana, but the same challenges affecting its development and implementation were identified.Conclusion The harmonised competency-based outcomes framework developed in this study serves as a starting point in ensuring the consistent production of high quality medical and dental graduates in Ghana. Implementation will require the regulator leading and monitoring individual institutions for compliance and providing support.

TI A Two-Year Regional Attitudinal Survey of Postgraduate Medical Trainees
   in North West England: A Regional Companion to National Benchmarking
SO JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND CURRICULAR DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE Postgraduate Medical Training; Trainee Experience; National Training
   Survey (GMC); Medical Education; Workplace Discrimination
AB Background The General Medical Council (GMC) National Training Survey (NTS) provides comprehensive national benchmarking of postgraduate medical training in the UK and has consistently highlighted high levels of satisfaction with supervision alongside persistent challenges relating to trainee wellbeing, discrimination, and workforce pressures. While invaluable, its national scope limits detailed interrogation of region-specific training processes and the evaluation of local interventions. This study reports a two-year regional trainee attitudinal survey from the North West of England, designed to supplement national GMC findings through increased granularity and to explore changes following local initiatives.Methods A structured, anonymous survey was distributed to all postgraduate medical trainees in the North West Deanery in 2023 and repeated in 2024. The questionnaire covered demographics, teaching and learning opportunities, supervisory support, usability of the new curricula, access to study budgets, and experiences of discrimination. Responses were analysed descriptively and compared across years. Findings were interpreted alongside GMC NTS results from 2023-2025.Results Responses were received from 166 trainees in 2023 and 151 in 2024. Modest numerical improvements in satisfaction with teaching opportunities and high, stable satisfaction with supervisory support were observed, consistent with national trends. The proportion of trainees working less-than-full-time increased significantly. Although numerical reductions in reported discrimination were seen following the introduction of bystander training, these changes were not statistically significant. Persistent challenges regarding study budget sufficiency and reimbursement were observed across both survey years.Conclusions This regional survey demonstrates trends aligned with national GMC findings while providing additional, deanery-level insight into locally modifiable aspects of training. Regional trainee surveys represent a valuable adjunct to national benchmarking by enabling contextualised interpretation of national data and cautious evaluation of local interventions.

DT Article
DE Q methodology; gifted students; T & Uuml;B & Idot;TAK 2204-A high school

AB Introduction: Research projects are important for encouraging students to think, arousing curiosity, conducting research and observation, producing solutions to problems, and developing 21st century skills. They are also important in terms of revealing the talents of gifted students. The limited number of studies in this field and the absence of Q method applications increases the importance of this study. The aim of the study is to examine the perceptions of gifted high school students who applied to the T & Uuml;B & Idot;TAK 2204-A project competition regarding project development using the Q method. Method: The Q methodology, one of the mixed methods, was used. The study group consisted of 25 gifted high school students attending the Science and Art Center in a provincial center in the Southeast Anatolia region during the 2024-2025 academic year. Findings: The findings showed that gifted students were grouped under two factors. Four students were not found in any factor, three students were found in the second factor, and 18 students were grouped in the first factor. Based on the Z-scores and order of importance of the items, the first item was "I want to devote time to the project because it contributes to my personal-academic development," the second was "I want to participate in the project," and the third is "I want to participate in the project with my teammates." In conclusion, gifted students had a positive attitude towards group work and collaboration and participate in the project process voluntarily. Discussion: It can be concluded that gifted students who participated in the project process benefitted from the projects in terms of their academic and personal development, participated in this process of their own volition, enjoyed group work, and did not hesitate to reapply even if their project applications were not accepted, indicating that they had high self-confidence.

   inclusive education
ID OF-FIT INDEXES; BEHAVIOR; STRATEGIES; PROGRAMS; STUDENTS
AB Introduction: Research has demonstrated that the use of evidence-based strategies in classroom management increases student engagement and academic achievement, reduces problem behaviors, and positively influences teachers' professional satisfaction by supporting their ability to manage classrooms effectively. To promote teachers' adoption of evidence-based classroom management strategies, it is essential first to determine the extent to which these strategies are being implemented. This study aims to develop a valid and reliable classroom management scale that can be used to assess the level at which primary school teachers working in inclusive educational settings employ classroom management strategies proven to be effective. Method: In this study, a scale development process was conducted. To determine whether the scale demonstrated adequate validity and reliability, both Classical Test Theory and Item Response Theory were employed. McDonald's omega, Cronbach's alpha, and marginal reliability analyses indicated that the overall reliability of the scale was high. Validity examinations based on Item Response Theory likewise yielded positive and consistent results. Discussion: The findings obtained in this study indicate that the developed scale can be used as a reliable and practical instrument to measure the extent to which primary school teachers working in inclusive educational settings employ evidence-based classroom management strategies. In this context, it is suggested that the Evidence-Based Classroom Management Scale (EBCMS) can be utilized in teacher education and in research related to teacher preparation and professional development.

AB Introduction: Various studies have demonstrated that individuals with special needs are at a higher risk of experiencing privacy violations compared to their typically developing peers. For individuals with special needs to acquire the necessary knowledge about privacy, educational interventions must be implemented to address issues related to privacy. At this point, special education teachers bear significant responsibilities. This study aims to examine the views and experiences of special education teachers regarding privacy education. Method: This study employed a phenomenological design, a qualitative research method. The study group consisted of 20 special education teachers. A semi-structured interview form was used to collect data. The interviews were conducted face-to-face. The obtained data were analyzed using the content analysis method. Findings: As a result of the analyses, four main themes were identified: the content of privacy education, privacy violations and coping methods, the instruction of privacy education in the classroom, and the level of family involvement. Discussion: The findings revealed that special education teachers had limited knowledge and skills regarding the content of privacy education, coping methods for privacy violations, and the instructional process. Additionally, the findings suggested that family collaboration during the privacy education process is insufficient, and the level of family involvement varies depending on several factors. The findings are consistent with the existing literature and support the need for structured programs for special education teachers as well as efforts aimed at increasing family participation.

TI Assessment of Job Satisfaction and Burnout Levels of Sports Trainers
   Working in Autism Sports Club Associations
SO ANKARA UNIVERSITESI EGITIM BILIMLERI FAKULTESI OZEL EGITIM
   DERGISI-ANKARA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES JOURNAL OF
   SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Autism; neurodevelopmental disorder; sports trainers; job satisfaction;
   burnout levels
ID LIFE SATISFACTION; TEACHERS; DIRECTIONS; PHILOSOPHY; COMMITMENT;
   ENGAGEMENT; RESOURCES; SYMPTOMS; EFFICACY; CHILDREN
AB Introduction: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that begins in early childhood and persists throughout life. This study aims to examine the job satisfaction and professional burnout levels of sports trainers providing services to individuals with ASD based on various variables (sex, age, years of experience). Method: The study included a total of 156 sports trainers working in autism sports club and associations, consisting of 79 females and 77 males. Participants completed a demographic information form, the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI), and the Minnesota Job Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ). Findings: No significant differences were found in the subscales of the MBI according to sex. However, depersonalization and personal accomplishment showed significant differences according to age, while personal accomplishment also differed significantly between trainers with 1-3 years and 7-9 years of experience. In the MSQ, significant differences were observed in the extrinsic satisfaction and general satisfaction subscales according to sex, and between the 20-25 age group and the 26-30 and 31+ age groups. However, no significant differences were found in job satisfaction levels based on years of experience. In the correlation analysis of the MBI and MSQ subscales, only personal accomplishment was found to be positively correlated with intrinsic, extrinsic, and general satisfaction. Discussion: As sports trainers age, their depersonalization and sense of personal accomplishment increase, and as their years of professional experience grow, their sense of personal accomplishment also improves. Male trainers reported higher external and general job satisfaction compared to female trainers. Additionally, job satisfaction levels increased with age but remained unaffected by years of experience. Furthermore, sports trainers working with individuals with ASD may exhibit emotionally detached behaviors due to excessive workload, and as their level of their intrinsic and extrinsic satisfaction decreases.

TI Social Skills Development in Special Education: The Role of Religious
   Culture and Moral Knowledge Textbooks in Special Education
SO ANKARA UNIVERSITESI EGITIM BILIMLERI FAKULTESI OZEL EGITIM
   DERGISI-ANKARA UNIVERSITY FACULTY OF EDUCATIONAL SCIENCES JOURNAL OF
   SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Religion education; social skills development; special education;
   religious culture and ethics (RCME); content analysis; empathy and moral
   values
ID COMPETENCE; STUDENTS
AB Introduction: This study aims to examine the potential of Religious Culture and Moral Education (RCME) textbooks to support the social skill development of students with special educational needs. Social skills constitute fundamental competencies that enable individuals to communicate effectively, sustain social relationships, and adapt to their environment. For students with special needs, it is critically important that these skills be reinforced through structured, concrete, and well-designed instructional processes.<br /> Method: The RCME textbooks used at the primary and lower secondary levels within the Ministry of National Education were analyzed through qualitative content analysis. Written content was systematically coded and categorized according to social skill themes, visual materials, activity samples, and explanatory texts. However, adaptations addressing the individualized learning needs of students with special needs remain limited. Revising textbooks to incorporate greater visual support, concrete activities, and individualized learning strategies would enhance the effectiveness of social skills education. Additionally, enabling teachers to make pedagogical modifications during instruction is essential for the sustainability of social skill acquisition. Integrating guidance practices that strengthen home-school collaboration may also provide a multidimensional learning environment that supports students' social development. This holistic approach enhances the continuity of the learning process and increases the potential for establishing lasting behavioral change.

   Skills: RDRWP

DT Article
DE Reading skills; speaking skills; book reading model (RDRWP); book clubs.
ID LITERATURE CIRCLES; FRAMEWORK
AB This study examined the effects of the RDRWP model on students' reading comprehension and speaking skills across middle and high school classrooms in T & uuml;rkiye. Grounded in constructivist theory, the model integrates book reading, discussion, collaboration, and project-based production, conceptualizing literacy learning as a socially mediated and interactive process. The study employed a mixed-methods design combining quantitative and qualitative data to provide a comprehensive understanding of the implementation and outcomes of the model. The quantitative strand adopted an experimental design to examine changes in students' reading comprehension and speaking performance, while the qualitative strand drew on semi-structured interviews with participating students and practicing teachers. Quantitative findings demonstrated that participation in the RDRWP model contributed positively to the development of students' reading comprehension and speaking skills. Qualitative findings further revealed that the model promoted active participation, collaborative interaction, and the development of a stronger reading culture within classrooms. Overall, the findings suggest that the RDRWP model provides a promising pedagogical framework for integrating reading, discussion, and collaborative meaning-making practices in literacy education.

TI Development of the Life Science Anxiety Scale: A Validity and
   Reliability Study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND FUTURE-EGITIM VE GELECEK DERGISI
LA English
DT Article
DE Life science; anxiety; scale development; primary school students
AB The level of anxiety experienced by students in a life science course can shape not only their academic performance but also their emotional development. Therefore, the aim of this study was to develop a scale for examining primary school students' anxiety about life science lessons. The study was conducted using a survey model, and the data were collected face-to-face. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were used to analyze the data. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was performed with 470 and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with the participation of 437 primary school students. Furthermore, the Cronbach Alpha reliability coefficient value of the scale was calculated as 0.85. The two-factor structure of the scale was confirmed by the CFA (x(2)/sd=2.08; RMSEA=0.050; SRMR=0.045; NFI=0.94; NNFI=0.96; CFI=0.97; GFI=0.95; AGFI=0.93). The study found that the scale is valid and reliable. The research suggested that the scale can be used to examine primary school students' anxiety about life science lessons.

TI The Mediating Role of Fear of the Future in the Association between
   Career Goal Inconsistency and Mental Health
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND FUTURE-EGITIM VE GELECEK DERGISI
LA English
DT Article
DE Career goal inconsistency; fear of the future; depression; anxiety;
   stress; loneliness
ID ANXIETY; UNCERTAINTY; DEPRESSION; STRESS
AB Uncertainty and inconsistency in university students' career goals may increase fear of the future and constitute an important risk factor for the emergence of psychological problems such as depression, anxiety, stress, and loneliness. This study aimed to examine the mediating role of fear of the future in the relationship between career goal inconsistency and depression, anxiety, stress, and loneliness among students studying at faculties of sport sciences. A correlational survey model was used in the study, and the data collected from 318 sport sciences students studying at universities in T & uuml;rkiye were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). In addition, the construct validity of the measurement instruments was evaluated through confirmatory factor analysis using chi 2, df, p, CFI, TLI, SRMR and RMSEA while their reliability was assessed using Cronbach's alpha coefficient. The findings indicated that career goal inconsistency was significantly associated with fear of the future and that fear of the future might play a mediating role in explaining the relationships between career goal inconsistency and depression, anxiety, stress, and loneliness. The model explained 45.4% of the variance in fear of the future, 47.9% in depression, 45.3% in anxiety, 41.5% in stress, and 27.7% in loneliness. These results highlighted the importance of career counseling and psychological support practices for sport sciences students.

TI The Image of the Teaching Profession from the Perspectives of Teachers,

DT Article
DE Image of the teaching profession; teacher; administrator; parent
AB The aim of the study is to analyze the image of the teaching profession from the perspective of its key stakeholders-administrators, teachers, and parents-and to reveal the similarities and differences in the perceptions of these groups. Furthermore, the findings of the study aim to contribute to the development of policies that strengthen the social status of the teaching profession. In addition, teachers' lack of self-care, the mismatch between theoretical knowledge and practice in undergraduate education, and social perception have also negatively affected this process.

TI Comparative Analysis of International Baccalaureate and Cambridge
   Chemistry Curriculum Based on the Revised Bloom's Taxonomy
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND FUTURE-EGITIM VE GELECEK DERGISI
LA English
DT Article
DE Chemistry curriculum; international baccalaureate organization;
   international cambridge education; revised Bloom's taxonomy
ID INTELLECTUAL DEMANDS; SCIENCE CURRICULUM; PROGRAM; QUESTIONS; SCHOOLS;
   CHINA
AB The aim of this study is to compare the learning objectives of the globally recognized International Baccalaureate Diploma Program (IBDP) and Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) Chemistry curricula according to the Revised Bloom's Taxonomy. In the study conducted through document analysis, 362 learning objectives in the IBDP and 353 learning objectives in the IGCSE were analyzed. The learning objectives were independently coded by two researchers according to the knowledge and cognitive process dimensions of Revised Bloom's Taxonomy (RBT), and discrepancies were resolved through discussion and expert consultation. The results were analyzed using frequency and percentage distributions. The results revealed that both curricula tended to emphasize the understand and apply levels within the cognitive process dimension, whereas objectives targeting the create category were scarce. In the knowledge dimension, conceptual and procedural knowledge were dominant in both curricula. However, notable differences emerged between the two programs. The IBDP included a higher proportion of learning objectives at the apply and evaluate levels, whereas the IGCSE curriculum contained more objectives at the remember and understand levels. These findings suggest that while both curricula prioritize conceptual understanding and the practical application of knowledge, the IBDP places greater emphasis on higher-order cognitive processes. By systematically mapping these cognitive disparities, this study provides an empirical benchmark to guide curriculum developers in bridging the gap between foundational chemistry education and advanced, higher-order skills.

TI Academic Experiences, Curriculum Perceptions, and Professional Readiness
   Among Dental Students in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
SO JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND CURRICULAR DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE dental education; academic experience; curriculum perception; research
   participation; community engagement; professional readiness; career
   expectations
ID SELF-PERCEIVED PREPAREDNESS; MOTIVATIONS; DENTISTRY; STRESS
AB Background Dental education is undergoing continuous development to align with evolving healthcare demands. Understanding students' academic experiences, curriculum perceptions, research involvement, and career expectations is essential for improving training quality. This study aimed to assess these factors among dental students. Methods This cross-sectional descriptive study included 194 dental students from the second year to the internship level. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Data were collected through a structured, self-administered questionnaire assessing academic experiences, curriculum perceptions, research involvement, community engagement, and career expectations. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were performed, with significance set at p < .05. Results Of the participants, 56.7% were female, and 43.3% reported having considered leaving dental school. Research involvement was reported by 40.7% of students, with lack of knowledge and time constraints identified as key barriers. Time-management difficulties were the most commonly reported academic challenge (33.0%). Perceptions of the curriculum were divided, with significant differences observed across academic levels (p = .020). Differences between preclinical and clinical training were reported by 48.5% of students (p < .001). Career expectations were generally high (65.5%), although they varied significantly across academic levels (p = .001). Conclusion Dental students reported varied academic experiences, with challenges in time management, research engagement, and clinical transition. These exploratory findings highlight the need for targeted educational support and further validation.

TI Effectiveness of Simulation-Based Training Versus Traditional Lecturing
   for Outbreak Investigation Among Medical Students: A Randomized
   Controlled Trial
SO JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND CURRICULAR DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE simulation-based training; outbreak investigation; medical education;
   randomized controlled trial; public health preparedness; cholera
   outbreak; tabletop exercise; traditional lecturing; knowledge and skills
   assessment; community medicine
ID EDUCATION
AB Introduction Training in outbreak investigation is essential for public health readiness. This study examines how simulation-based training improves medical students' outbreak investigation skills compared to conventional lecture techniques. Methods We conducted a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) at Combined Military Hospital (CMH) Lahore Medical College over an eleven-month period. Participants were recruited from 4th-year MBBS students without any prior outbreak investigation training. Participants were randomized to control (lecture) (n = 45) and intervention (simulation) (n = 42) groups. Simulation-based training involving a Cholera outbreak scenario was compared to traditional lecture-based teaching. Pre and post-intervention assessments were used to measure knowledge, skills, and attitudes. Statistical analyses included t-tests and descriptive statistics. Results Simulation-based training resulted in a significantly greater improvement in knowledge and skills compared to the control group (p < 0.001). No statistically significant improvement in attitudes was observed (p = 0.068 within simulation group; p = 0.866 between groups).Discussion Simulation-based training was associated with greater improvement in knowledge and skills than traditional lecture-based teaching, while no significant difference was observed in attitudes. Although both groups showed increases in scores, simulation-based training was associated with greater improvement in knowledge and skills related to outbreak investigation. The outcomes specify that in order to achieve complex learning requirements, medical education needs a variety of scholastic approaches. Conclusion Simulation-based training was associated with greater improvement in knowledge and skills compared to traditional teaching. To augment educational outcomes and qualify aspiring healthcare professionals for real-world challenges, preceptors should think about incorporating simulation-based training into their curriculum.

TI TIMES AND SPACES OF TEACHER EDUCATION AT THE UNIVERSITY OF SÃO PAULO
SO REVISTA ON LINE DE POLITICA E GESTAO EDUCACIONAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Teacher education; Institutional policy; Social institution;
   Neoliberalism
AB This article presents an institutional overview of the University of S & atilde;o Paulo, with the aim of analyzing educational policies over the past two decades. Based on an interpretive and critical reading grounded in historical-dialectical materialism, the study sought to understand teacher education in order to identify directions that align with the neoliberal perspective on education, as well as areas of resistance to this perspective. The research corpus consists of a documentary analysis structured around three axes: state and national regulations and their impacts on institutional teacher education policies at USP; the management of the Office of the Dean of Undergraduate Studies from 2002 to 2025, between the instituted and the instituting; and institutional programs in teaching, research, outreach, student retention, and student inclusion. TI AI-DRIVEN CHALLENGES IN TECHNICAL HIGHER EDUCATION: AN INSTITUTIONAL
   PERSPECTIVE
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE higher education; artificial intelligence; engineering education;
   digital technologies; academic integrity
ID ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE
AB The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is substantially transforming higher education, particularly in technical universities that prepare specialists for high-tech industries. AI tools enable personalised learning, automate assessment, and enhance educational analytics, while simultaneously generating new pedagogical and ethical challenges. The aim of this study is to identify the key problems associated with the application of AI technologies in higher technical education institutions and to analyse their impact on teaching and learning processes. The research employs a mixed-methods approach that combines a review of the scholarly literature with an empirical investigation conducted through an online survey of 1,916 students and 515 faculty members. In addition, the authors carried out a supplementary survey in cooperation with student self-government bodies regarding the key AI tools used by students in the course of their studies; the sample of this supplementary survey comprised 378 respondents. The results show that AI is widely used by students, primarily for information retrieval, idea generation, and text production, while its application in complex analytical tasks remains limited. A significant gap was identified between students and faculty in the adoption of AI. Furthermore, the findings highlight problems related to academic integrity, the decline of independent learning, and the absence of a clear institutional policy regulating the use of AI. The study concludes that the integration of AI into higher technical education is systemic in nature and requires the development of institutional policies, the transformation of teaching methods, and the enhancement of digital competencies among both faculty and students.

TI CONTROLLED AI SUPPORT IN LITERATURE REVIEW WRITING: STUDENT PERCEPTIONS,
   TEXTUAL FEATURES, AND ETHICAL AWARENESS
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE AI-assisted writing; literature review writing; academic writing
   instruction; student perceptions; ethical awareness; academic integrity
AB Purpose. This study examines how controlled AI support influences students' perceptions and written texts in brief literature review writing. The purpose was to compare non-AI and AI-supported writing conditions in terms of synthesis, evaluation, ownership, perceived learning, ethical awareness, and linguistic features of student-written paragraphs. Method. The study used a mixed-methods research design. The sample included 65 higher education students from two university contexts; 37 participants were BA-level students and 28 were Master's/PhD-level students. The intervention consisted of an academic writing workshop followed by two source-based literature review paragraph tasks: one completed without AI support and one completed with controlled AI support. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire, open-ended reflection questions, AI-use disclosure items, ethical-awareness scenarios, and student-written paragraphs. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, frequencies and percentages, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for paired comparisons, and Mann-Whitney U tests for academic-level comparisons. Open-ended responses were analysed thematically, and student-written paragraphs were examined through linguistic and rhetorical feature analysis. Findings. Students perceived AI as useful for synthesis, organisation, language improvement, and producing a stronger paragraph. However, non-AI writing was associated with stronger ownership and learning. AI-supported texts contained more synthesis markers, evaluative markers, hedging markers, explicit source references, and source-specific details. Ethical awareness was partial, especially regarding undisclosed AI-generated writing and AI-added references. Implications for research and practice. The findings support controlled AI integration in academic writing instruction. AI can serve as a scaffold for language, structure, and comparison, but explicit teaching of synthesis, evaluation, disclosure, and academic integrity remains necessary.

TI GenAI MINDS FOR HIGHER EDUCATION: READING AND EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE generative artificial intelligence; ChatGPT; Gemini; Claude; DeepSeek;
   Qwen; higher education; reading competence; emotional intelligence;
   sustainable AI use
AB This study examines how five generative AI systems (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek and Qwen) respond to questionnaires commonly used in higher education to assess reading-related and emotional dimensions in human learners, with the aim of informing more sustainable classroom use. Given the high water and electricity consumption associated with intensive GenAI use in universities, optimising tool selection based on response effectiveness is increasingly necessary. Using a descriptive quantitative approach, the Metacognitive Awareness Inventory (MAI) and the Wong-Law Emotional Intelligence Scale (WLEIS) were applied as human-oriented questionnaires. The analysis focuses on the degree of alignment between AI-generated answers and predefined reference response patterns. Results show clear differences among systems. Gemini and ChatGPT exhibited comparatively stable alignment in reading-related items, particularly in attention and memory, while Qwen showed the lowest overall deviation in both reading-related and emotional self-report items. Claude and DeepSeek displayed greater variability across both domains. These findings suggest that response consistency and task-specific alignment may serve as practical criteria for selecting generative AI tools in higher education, supporting pedagogical effectiveness while contributing to more environmentally responsible digital practices aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.

TI AI-ASSISTED LEARNING MATERIALS DEVELOPMENT FOR ESP: AFFORDANCES AND
   LIMITATIONS
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE AI-assisted learning materials development; AI-assisted learning
   content; ESP; Technology Acceptance Model; AI literacy; regulatory
   frameworks; higher education
AB Generative artificial intelligence has moved rapidly from a novelty to a routine part of how many English for Specific Purposes (ESP) teachers prepare their materials, yet the normative and empirical picture of how these tools should be used has not kept pace. This article examines AI-assisted learning materials development for ESP from three complementary angles: the legal, ethical, and competency-based frameworks that govern AI use in the European Union and Ukraine; the existing research literature on AI-assisted materials development; and empirical evidence from ESP practitioners themselves. The study followed a three-stage mixed-methods design: an analysis of normative documents, including the EU AI Act, Ukrainian copyright and academic integrity legislation, EU and UNESCO ethics guidelines, and digital and AI competency frameworks; a literature review of Web of Science records screened for relevance; and a questionnaire administered to 46 ESP teachers at Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute, analysed through the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The normative analysis shows that, despite differing legal mechanisms, EU and Ukrainian frameworks converge on requiring human oversight, transparency, and disclosure of AI-generated content. The literature review confirms that AI tools increase efficiency and personalisation in materials development while introducing risks to quality, bias, and disciplinary accuracy, a tension sharper in ESP than in general education because of the field's dependence on precise, discipline-specific content and language. The survey results show that AI tool use is near-universal among the sampled teachers (95.7%), concentrated in vocabulary, grammar, and field-specific text generation. TAM analysis confirms all four hypothesised relationships between perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, attitude, and behavioural intention, with behavioural intention rated highest and time savings receiving the highest rating among the perceived usefulness items; notably, teachers were less positive about the time required to refine AI-generated output before classroom use. Perceived quality varied across exercise types, favouring open, communicative tasks over tightly structured ones, and self-assessed AI competency remains concentrated at the basic level, particularly for AI ethics. These findings indicate that current ESP practice is best described as AI-assisted rather than AI-driven, with teachers retaining a central evaluative role consistent with normative requirements, though a literacy gap, especially in ethics, remains the main obstacle to confident AI-assisted materials development. TI GENERATIVE AI IN EFL LEARNING: ATTITUDES OF CZECH AND SLOVAK STUDENTS AT
   THE TERTIARY LEVEL
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE generative AI; university EFL learners; language skills; generative AI
   challenges and drawbacks
AB This paper aims to provide a comprehensive examination of the perceptions of Czech and Slovak English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners regarding the integration of generative AI (artificial intelligence) tools into their English language learning process. The research method used in this study was a self-report questionnaire with a Likert scale. It included three types of statements: general generative AI, English language generative AI, and challenges-related generative AI statements. Through a rigorous quantitative analysis of survey data performed in the open-source application for statistical calculations JASP, the study elucidates that the research participants, who comprised Czech and Slovak university EFL students, predominantly regard generative AI as a transformative, time-efficient, and impactful educational resource that significantly enhances their learning experiences, promotes autonomy, and facilitates overall language development. Despite acknowledging these benefits, participants express concerns about the potential challenges, especially the risk of providing inaccurate responses, its possible influence on critical thinking or creativity, as well as feedback quality compared to traditional teacher guidance, or its underuse for the development of speaking and pronunciation. Interestingly, the study suggests statistically significant disparities between Czech and Slovak students in two respects: their perceptions of the emotional and empathetic limitations of generative AI tools (p-value = 0.022) and their approach to pronunciation practice (p-value = 0.035), with Slovak learners scoring higher on both. These findings reveal a complex landscape of attitudes; while many students enthusiastically embrace generative AI as an invaluable asset, others show reluctance to fully commit, highlighting a pressing need for deeper investigation into the factors that influence their willingness to engage with AI technologies in education. This study not only enriches the discourse on the pedagogical implications of generative AI but also emphasises the need to address the inherent challenges it poses to maximise its potential for language learning.

TI THE ROLE OF AI-POWERED TOOLS IN EFL TEACHER EDUCATION: EXPLORING
   MOTIVATION, ENGAGEMENT, AND SELF-EFFICACY OF TEACHER CANDIDATES
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE EFL; teacher candidates; AI; motivation; engagement; self-efficacy;
   teacher education
ID LANGUAGE
AB Focusing on the integration of AI-powered tools in EFL (English as a Foreign Language) teacher preparation, this mixed-methods study investigated the impact of these tools on the motivation, engagement, and self-efficacy of 150 teacher candidates. The researchers gathered quantitative data from a survey and qualitative data through in-depth interviews with 10 participants. The results revealed a strong interconnection between motivation, engagement, and self-efficacy. The study also showed that the use of AI tools was instrumental in enhancing students' self--efficacy. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the factors that influence learner motivation. Key factors associated with teaching confidence included the combination of intrinsic and extrinsic motivation and the use of AI tools. Participants generally perceived AI tools as effective in providing timely feedback and creating interactive exercises that supported their confidence and engagement. However, they also emphasized that hands-on classroom experience remains necessary for becoming fully prepared teachers.

TI SELF-REGULATED WRITING STRATEGIES IN AI-ENHANCED ACADEMIC WRITING:
   INSIGHTS FROM INDONESIAN EFL DOCTORAL STUDENTS
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE academic writing; artificial intelligence; EFL doctoral students; higher
   education; self-regulated writing strategies
AB This article reports on self-regulated writing strategies in AI-enhanced academic writing among EFL doctoral students in Indonesia. The study aimed to identify the level of strategy use and to examine its application, as well as the challenges and solutions, across the stages of the academic writing process. A mixed-methods design was employed, combining a survey of 54 EFL doctoral students and semi-structured interviews with six participants from a public university in Indonesia. Quantitative findings showed a high level of self-regulated writing strategies, particularly in motivational self-talk, goal monitoring and evaluating, text processing, idea planning, emotional control, feedback handling, and interest enhancement, while course memory was moderate. These results suggest strong self-awareness and autonomy in sustaining motivation, organizing ideas, monitoring progress, and regulating emotions. Qualitative data revealed that students engaged in a systematic, cyclical writing process encompassing planning, execution, and evaluation, with writer-generated ideas enhanced by AI during planning, writer control, voice preservation, and feedback during execution, and self-monitoring and critical review during evaluation. Despite the benefits, challenges stemming from AI's limitations in personal and contextual writing persist, prompting students to adopt critical, controlled use of AI as a practical solution. This study provides insights into EFL doctoral students' self-regulated writing and their critical, controlled use of AI to address its limitations.

TI THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN TRAINING CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS
   SPECIALISTS
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE digital technologies; traditional instruction; higher education;
   critical thinking; learning competencies; generative models
AB Rationale. The relevance of this study is driven by the need for effective integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the training of crisis communications specialists in the context of educational digitalization, and the persistence of methodological, ethical, and organizational barriers. Objective. The study aimed to determine how the integration of artificial intelligence contributes to the development of professional and analytical competencies among students in the field of crisis communications. Methods. The research combined theoretical analysis, an empirical student survey, and an expert survey of faculty members as key informants. Results. The findings revealed that AI integration into the training of crisis communications specialists was systematic yet uneven, depending on institutional conditions and the digital maturity of the participants. Usage patterns ranged from episodic to comprehensive, with over 70% of students employing AI regularly as both an automation tool and a cognitive partner. Three integration models were identified: auxiliary (49.3%), integrated (34.8%), and transformative (15.9%). Students utilized generative models, analytical systems, and simulation platforms. Following AI integration, improvements were observed in analytical skills (3.1 -> 4.2), decision-making speed (3.3 -> 4.4), critical thinking (3.5 -> 4.0), and communicative skills (3.4 -> 4.1). At the same time, a partial "cognitive delegation" effect was identified. Referential comparison with traditional instruction indicated the potential viability of a blended approach: AI use was associated with enhanced task performance efficiency, whereas traditional methods were linked to deeper conceptual understanding. The primary barriers to integration were personnel-related, ethical, cognitive, and resource-based constraints. Implications. The findings may be utilized by faculty, university administrators, and educational program developers.

TI NEGOTIATING ACADEMIC WRITING IN AN AI-INFUSED COURSE: STUDENTS'
   REFLECTIVE NARRATIVES OF AI USE AND AUTHORIAL RESPONSIBILITY
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic Integrity; AI-Infused Academic Writing; EFL; Ethical Awareness;
   Indonesian Higher Education; Pedagogical Scaffolding; Reflective
   Narratives
AB AI-infused academic writing has transformed students' academic literacy practices in higher education. Although research on AI and academic writing continues to grow, many studies still focus primarily on the effectiveness of AI tools and writing products, while students' interpretations of their learning experiences and their negotiation of AI use in academic writing remain underexplored. Viewing academic writing as a social practice, this study aimed to explore how students narrated their learning experiences and negotiated the use of AI while maintaining authorial responsibility in an AI-infused academic writing course. This study employed a qualitative approach using thematic analysis of reflective narratives. Data were collected through reflective written narratives from four undergraduate students who attended an academic writing course over one semester. The data were analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns related to students' experiences of learning academic writing, their use of AI, and their sense of authorship and responsibility. The findings revealed that students narrated the course as an initial and formative space for developing academic writing competence and academic identity. AI was described as providing cognitive and procedural support that assisted students in understanding concepts, generating initial ideas, and writing more efficiently. However, students also negotiated the boundaries of AI use by emphasizing writer control, academic responsibility, and ethical awareness. The findings provide exploratory, context-specific insights into how students experienced academic writing and negotiated AI use in one course setting. This study highlights the importance of positioning AI as pedagogical scaffolding that supports reflective learning and responsible academic writing practices.

AB This paper focuses on artificial intelligence tools that may support e-scaffolding practices during listening activities in ESP instruction at universities in Ukraine and Israel. Attention is paid to the analysis of key concepts in e-scaffolding. The study of listening skills development at universities is attracting growing interest due to the increasing need for future professionals capable of effective communication, with listening as a necessary skill. This exploratory survey-based study examined ESP teachers' use of AI-supported e scaffolding in listening instruction at universities in Ukraine and Israel. Seventy teachers participated in the study, including 50 from Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute and 20 from Western Galilee College and Technion-Israel Institute of Technology. At the same time, the paper approaches claims regarding students' listening improvement cautiously, as the results are based primarily on teachers' observations and self-reported perceptions rather than independently assessed student outcomes. The study suggests that integrating AI tools with e-scaffolding strategies may contribute to more adaptive and flexible English language teaching practices in higher education. The findings also highlight the perceived potential of AI-supported instruction to address challenges in language learning, digital competence, and the evolving educational needs of contemporary society.

TI ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-POWERED WRITING TOOL PAPERPAL FOR ENGAGING PHD
   STUDENTS IN ACADEMIC WRITING
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence; academic writing; PhD students; foreign
   language education; engagement; Paperpal
AB Purpose. Doctoral students writing in English as a foreign language frequently encounter linguistic, rhetorical, and affective challenges that undermine engagement and progress on their dissertations. Although artificial intelligence-powered writing tools (AI-PWTs) are increasingly used in higher education, empirical evidence regarding their pedagogical integration at the doctoral level remains limited. This study examines PhD students' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI tools and assesses the potential contribution of integrating Paperpal into an Academic Writing course. Method. A mixed-methods classroom-based case study was conducted with 42 PhD students at a Ukrainian pedagogical university. Quantitative data were collected through two structured surveys and pre-and post-intervention evaluation of writing drafts assessed across seven criteria. Paired-samples t-tests were used to examine within-subject changes. Qualitative data were obtained from open-ended questions in surveys, reflective accounts, and a SWOT analysis and analysed thematically. Findings. Results indicate widespread, but predominantly unsystematic, use of general-purpose AI tools prior to the intervention. Following structured integration of Paperpal, statistically significant improvements in the analysed writing samples were observed across all seven criteria, with the largest improvement in ethical AI use. Participants reported increased motivation, greater confidence, and more responsible AI practices. Implications for research and practice. The findings suggest that AI-PWTs can function as formative scaffolds in doctoral writing pedagogy when embedded within structured instruction and ethical guidance. The study provides empirical evidence supporting the integration of supervised AI in postgraduate education and highlights the need for institutional frameworks, digital literacy training, and longitudinal research.

TI FACULTY MEMBERS' EXPERIENCES WITH AI IN LANGUAGE TEACHING: A PEDAGOGICAL
   PERSPECTIVE
SO ADVANCED EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence; foreign language education; pedagogical
   integration; faculty experiences; higher education; professional
   identity
ID ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE; CONTENT KNOWLEDGE
AB The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) in language education has created new expectations for educators while simultaneously introducing pedagogical, institutional, and professional challenges. However, existing research has predominantly focused on technological tool effectiveness and learner outcomes, leaving faculty members' lived experiences and instructional adaptations comparatively underexplored. This study aims to explore faculty members' experiences with AI in higher education language teaching and to examine the difficulties they encounter when integrating these technologies into instructional practices in pedagogically meaningful ways. The study employed a qualitative research design to examine participants' experiences and the challenges they encountered. Participants were 12 faculty members working at Schools of Foreign Languages in three public universities in T & uuml;rkiye. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews focusing on AI use, instructional practices, institutional conditions, and professional perceptions. The interviews were transcribed and analysed using thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns and shared experiences related to AI-supported teaching. The findings revealed a clear gap between technological familiarity and pedagogical integration. Although faculty members reported being able to use AI tools functionally for preparation, material development, and productivity-related tasks, they experienced difficulties in aligning these tools with learning outcomes, classroom interaction, and assessment practices. Institutional constraints, limited infrastructural support, workload pressures, ethical concerns, and varying levels of student readiness further shaped their engagement with AI-supported instruction. The results also indicated that AI integration influences teachers' professional roles, creating tensions related to authority, control, and professional identity in technology-mediated learning environments. Overall, the study suggests that effective AI integration requires more than technical competence; it demands pedagogical guidance, institutional coordination, and the development of AI literacy among both educators and students. The findings have implications for teacher education, professional development, and institutional policy, emphasising the need for structured support, discipline-sensitive instructional models, and clear ethical frameworks. Future research should focus on developing pedagogically grounded AI practices and institutional strategies that enable sustainable and context-responsive integration of AI in language education.

This study investigates how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) influences L2 instructors' perceptions of creativity and effectiveness in lesson planning and material design for writing instruction. It also examines factors motivating continued or discontinued use of GenAI. While participants reported using several GenAI tools, ChatGPT clearly emerged as the dominant one. Method. A mixed-methods research design was used. Data were collected from adult L2 instructors in Canadian tertiary programs using survey and semi-structured interviews. The survey included closed- and open-ended questions, while interviews provided deeper insights into instructors' experiences with GenAI tools. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics for quantitative responses and thematic analysis for qualitative data. Findings. The findings reveal that GenAI plays a dual, context-dependent role. Most participants reported that GenAI influenced their creativity, particularly by supporting idea generation, material development, and pedagogical innovation. However, concerns about overreliance, reduced originality, and formulaic outputs were also reported. The impact on effectiveness was more conditional, with benefits in time management, customization, and teaching capacity balanced by challenges such as prompting complexity, the need for editing, and variable output quality. Decisions to continue or discontinue GenAI use were influenced by practical benefits, professional growth, and ethical and financial concerns. Implications for research and practice. The study highlights the importance of AI literacy, institutional support, and critical engagement for effective GenAI implementation. It suggests that GenAI should be used as a collaborative tool. Future research should explore long-term impacts and include diverse educational contexts and learner outcomes.

TI Dual Language for Whom? A Critical Race Spatial Analysis of Programming
   Allocation for Multilingual Learners in Texas
SO AERA OPEN
LA English
DT Article
DE immigration/immigrants; bilingual/bicultural; critical theory;
   demography; two-way dual language; critical race spatial analysis;
   bilingual programming; multilingual learners; one-way dual language
ID BILINGUAL-EDUCATION; 2-WAY IMMERSION; UNITED-STATES; WHITENESS;
   POLICIES; EQUITY; REFORM; LEGAL
AB The growing population of multilingual learners (MLs) in the United States has increased demand for bilingual education, particularly two-way dual language (TWDL) and one-way dual language (OWDL) programs. While TWDL programs are designed to serve both MLs and English-dominant students, OWDL programs primarily center MLs, using both the home language and English to support development. Although TWDL was originally intended to promote equity, it has increasingly been taken up as a form of educational marketization that attracts white, English-dominant families, often marginalizing the students whose linguistic resources make these programs possible. Using critical race spatial analysis (CRSA), this study examines the placement of TWDL and OWDL programs across Texas in relation to immigrant density, urbanicity, and socioeconomic factors. Findings show that TWDL programs cluster in more affluent, lower-immigrant areas, while OWDL programs are concentrated in higher-immigrant, lower-income communities, raising important questions about equity and access.

TI Educational Labor Migrations and the Suturing of Forgotten Places:
   Puerto Rican Teachers, Oklahoma City Schools, and the Ongoing Networks
   of Colonialism
SO BERKELEY REVIEW OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE colonialism; education; labor; migration; Oklahoma; Puerto Rico
ID TESTIMONIO
AB In 2014, Puerto Rican educators were recruited to teach in Oklahoma City Schools. What resulted in a seemingly small labor migration illuminates a deeper understanding of the actual relations among colonial experiments. It functions as no minor illustration of the centrality of educational labor experiments to the militaristic, capitalist, and other relations between the United States and its occupied territories. In this article, we observe educators as migrant laborers, whose lives are shaped by a nexus of colonial forces and whose labors and migrations suture two "forgotten places" (Gilmore, 2008) through new formations. We seek to understand how a "fly-over" state and an archipelagic possession are both related and central to educational colonization, how educational colonization is a labor project, and how all of this maps emergent analytic possibilities. How does this labor migration help us understand the unlikely interplay of two contexts in the colonial project? Through news articles, testimonio, ethnographic interludes, and archival data, we examine how we might newly understand the role of education and educators in the larger network of colonial relations.
