TI MIND THE GENDER GAP: ENTREPRENEURIAL MINDSET AMONG SPORTS MANAGEMENT
   MASTER'S STUDENTS WITH ENTREPRENEURIAL EXPERIENCE
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE higher education; experiential pedagogy; leadership competencies;
   innovation skills; student entrepreneurship; inclusive learning
   environments
ID SELF-EFFICACY; INTENTIONS; EDUCATION
AB This study investigates gender differences in the entrepreneurial mindset (EM) amongsports management Master's students with prior entrepreneurial exposure. A total of 350 students participated by completing an adapted version of the Scale to Assess Social Entrepreneurship Competency. The instrument was validated through exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, supporting a six-factor structure-Creativity and Innovation, Risk-taking, Strategic Leadership, Goal Orientation, Action-based Learning, and Ethical Responsibility-which explained 64.3% of the total variance (CFI = 0.93, TLI = 0.91, RMSEA = 0.048). Multivariate analysis of variance revealed significant gender differences (Wilks' Lambda = 0.84, F(6, 340) = 10.21, eta 2 = 0.15). Male students reported higher levels of Risk-taking, Strategic Leadership, and Goal Orientation, whereas no significant differences were found in Creativity and Innovation, Action-based Learning, or Ethical Responsibility. Regression analyses indicated that entrepreneurial background positively predicted Risk-taking and Strategic Leadership, while sports experience showed a marginal association with Goal Orientation. Gender emerged as the most consistent predictor across models. These findings underline persistent gender disparities in EM and emphasize the importance of gender-responsive educational strategies, including mentorship and experiential learning, to foster inclusive entrepreneurial development in higher education contexts.

TI ENVIRONMENTAL LITERACY DEVELOPMENT IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE CLASSROOMS: A
   QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL STUDY
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE environmental literacy; sustainability education; quasi-experimental
   research; interdisciplinary education
AB In the context of increasing global emphasis on sustainability education, integrating environmental competences into foreign language instruction represents an important interdisciplinary strategy. This study examines the effectiveness of a structured educational intervention aimed at developing environmental literacy in intermediate-level English language classrooms. A quantitative quasi-experimental design with a pre-test/post-test structure was implemented. The study involved 70 undergraduate students enrolled in English language courses at "Ion Creang & abreve;" State Pedagogical University of Chisin & abreve;u. Environmental literacy was assessed using a structured environmental literacy questionnaire measuring knowledge, attitudes, and skills, complemented by a structured environmental knowledge test. The intervention lasted eight weeks and integrated sustainability-related content through Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL), Task-Based Learning, and Project-Based Learning strategies. Statistical analysis using mixed ANOVA and independent samples t-tests revealed significant improvements in overall environmental literacy and in all measured dimensions. Effect size indicators demonstrated large practical effects, confirming the meaningful impact of the intervention. The results indicate that the deliberate integration of sustainability topics into language instruction is associated with significant gains in students' environmental literacy. While linguistic proficiency was not formally measured, the pedagogical integration suggests a viable pathway for interdisciplinary instruction. Additionally, it illustrates that language instruction can promote interdisciplinary collaboration in accordance with the tenets of instruction for Sustainable Development (ESD). In this perspective, the study underscores the current and prospective significance of language education in enhancing awareness and fostering responsible attitudes towards sustainability objectives. The investigation is carried out within the research project "Integrating and promoting green education in the initial training of English language teachers," strategic priorities: societal challenges, strategic direction: Innovative Educational Technologies and Products, with the code 25.80012.0807.56SE, which studies integrated approaches to green education in English language learning contexts.

TI SELF-PERCEPTION OF TEACHERS' EXPERIENCE AND KNOWLEDGE ON THE USE OF
   ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY IN EDUCATION IN SERBIA
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE assistive technology; special education; developmental disabilities;
   knowledge; experience
AB Assistive Technology (AT) is a vital tool for adapting educational programs to the specific needs of children with developmental disabilities due to its growing accessibility. However, its successful implementation depends on teachers' knowledge and prior experience within the school setting. This research surveyed 203 participants in order to compare how mainstream and special education teachers perceive their own AT skills. A translated and modified version of The Questionnaire of Teachers' Knowledge on the Use of Assistive Technology was used in order to collect the relevant data. The results indicate only partial familiarity with the usage of AT in schools. There were no significant differences found regarding stress, time requirements, impact on student achievement and the years of experience, however special educators perceive their knowledge to be greater than teachers employed in mainstream schools. These findings indicate that education, training and cooperation between both institutions are imperative and should be facilitated via established resource centres. By integrating AT, children with special needs can acquire necessary lifelong skills, expand vocational opportunities, and improve their overall inclusion in society.

SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE gamification; digital applications; higher education educational
   process; computer games; game models
AB The article outlines the content, functions, elements, and goals of gamification, as well as the importance of game models, video games, computer games, and digital applications in higher education. The main elements of the gamification structure are highlighted. The advantages and risks of using gamification in higher education are discussed. TI THE INFLUENCE OF GRIT ON PRIMARY SCHOOL TEACHERS' ABILITY TO MANAGE
   STRESS
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE grit; occupational stress; primary school teachers; Romania; modular
   school-year structure
ID GOAL-STRUCTURE
AB Teachers' occupational stress is an important topic in educational research, with implications for their well-being and performance. This study analysed the relationship between grit, defined as passion and perseverance for long-term goals, and the perception of occupational stress among primary school teachers in Romania, in the context of school year reorganisation from 2 semesters to 5 modules. This exploratory cross-sectional study included a sample of 158 primary education teachers from the northwestern region of Romania. Work-related stress was assessed through a questionnaire adapted from School Teachers Job Stressor Scale (Naono-Nagatomo et al., 2019), and the grit level was measured using the scale developed by Duckworth (2016). The results revealed differentiated levels of occupational stress, the highest being associated with the reorganisation of the academic year. The correlation analysis indicated significant negative relationships between grit levels and certain stress dimensions, particularly self-assessment of professional skills and peer relations, while the relationship with the overall stress was not significant. The qualitative data supported these findings, suggesting that grit facilitates stress management in specific contexts without equally influencing all dimensions of work-related stress. These preliminary findings emphasise the multidimensional nature of occupational stress and highlight the need for future research with larger, more representative samples to replicate and extend these associations.

TI INCLUSIVE PRACTICE AND ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY: SPECIAL EDUCATORS'
   PERSPECTIVES IN SERBIA
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE inclusive education; inclusion; special education; assistive technology
AB Assistive technology represents an integral part of contemporary approaches in special education practice and is recognized within the system of inclusive education. In recent years, 13 resource centers in Serbia have been established to support children with developmental disabilities and their families in AT implementation. The aim of this study was to examine the attitudes and self-reported perceptions of competence, barriers, and beliefs of special educators employed in resource centers regarding the use of assistive technology in their practice. The study used the Attitude Towards Assistive Technology Scale and a custom-designed questionnaire assessing competencies, beliefs, and perceived barriers to AT use. The sample included 110 participants. The attitudes of special educators toward the use of assistive technology were predominantly positive. Regarding their self-reported perceptions related to AT use, a positive perception of its benefits was observed, as well as the identification of areas that represent challenges and limitations in its application. Most participants expressed a need for additional professional development in this field. Special educators hold positive attitudes toward the use of assistive technology and report diverse self-reported perceptions of competence, barriers, and beliefs related to AT implementation. There is a need for further education, access to relevant information, and improved availability of resources.

TI FROM STEREOTYPES TO CARE: NURSING STUDENTS' PERCEPTIONS OF OLDER ADULTS'
   SUBJECTIVE MENTAL HEALTH AND DEPRESSION SEVERITY
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE nursing students; older adults; attitudes toward aging; mental health in
   older adults; depression in later life
ID ATTITUDES; PEOPLE; WORK
AB Population ageing is one of the most significant demographic transformations of the 21st century, creating new challenges for healthcare systems and nursing education worldwide. As the proportion of older adults continues to rise, understanding how future healthcare professionals perceive ageing becomes increasingly important. Nursing students' attitudes toward older adults may influence both the quality of care provided to this population and students' willingness to pursue careers in geriatric nursing. The present study examines nursing students' perceptions of older adults' mental health, quality of life, and depression symptoms. The present study employed a quantitative design. However, to complement and strengthen the quantitative findings, a random subsample of five participants from each group was selected to participate in in-depth qualitative interviews. Sixty nursing students enrolled in an academic nursing program in central Israel participated in the quantitative phase of the study. Participants completed two validated instruments: the Mental Health Continuum-Short Form (MHC-SF), assessing emotional, social, and psychological aspects of mental health, and the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), assessing four categories of depression symptoms. Quantitative data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA, Pearson correlations, and multiple regression analyses. In addition, interviews with a subgroup of nursing students provided deeper insight into their perceptions of ageing and well-being in later life. The findings indicate that nursing students did not differentiate significantly between emotional, social, and psychological dimensions of older adults' mental health, suggesting that mental wellbeing in later life is often perceived as a unified construct rather than a multidimensional one. In contrast, students did distinguish between different types of depression symptoms, perceiving depressed affect and somatic or retarded activity as more prominent indicators of depression than absence of positive affect or interpersonal difficulties. Overall, the study highlights the importance of strengthening gerontological education in nursing programs. Increasing students' clinical exposure to older adults and enhancing training in recognizing diverse mental health and depression symptoms may help reduce age-related stereotypes and promote more balanced professional attitudes toward ageing populations.

TI GENDER-RELATED DIFFERENCES IN POSTURAL MALALIGNMENT AND MUSCULOSKELETAL
   PAIN AMONG BORDER POLICE OFFICERS: IMPLICATIONS FOR PHYSICAL TRAINING
   CURRICULA AND OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH EDUCATION
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE postural malalignment; gender differences; postural body angles;
   musculoskeletal pain; occupational health. INTRODUCTION
ID LUMBAR LORDOSIS; RELIABILITY
AB This study aimed to investigate gender-related differences in postural malalignment and musculoskeletal pain by analyzing postural body angles, their associations with anthropometric and occupational variables, and the intercorrelations between postural parameters and pain intensity in a group of 82 police officers employed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Romania. Using a cross-sectional observational design, significant gender differences were identified in anthropometric and occupational characteristics. Significant gender-related differences were observed in postural alignment and musculoskeletal pain patterns, with females presenting greater cervical and pelvic malalignment, whereas males demonstrated greater thoracic spine length and knee flexion angle values. These findings support the concept of global postural malalignment as an integrated biomechanical phenomenon and highlight the importance of gender-specific approaches in postural assessment, prevention, and rehabilitation practice in occupational settings. The educational significance of the present study resides in its potential to support the development of evidence-based physical training curricula, ergonomic education initiatives, and preventive physical therapy programs within law-enforcement institutions. By identifying gender-specific patterns of postural malalignment and musculoskeletal symptoms, the findings provide relevant information for the design of targeted educational and corrective interventions aimed at promoting postural health, preventing musculoskeletal dysfunction, and enhancing occupational readiness among border police officers. Furthermore, the results may provide valuable insights for occupational health education by informing gender-sensitive approaches to postural assessment, injury prevention, and rehabilitation, which are associated with the promotion of long-term physical well-being and professional performance among personnel exposed to sustained occupational demands. Importantly, the findings of the present study will be incorporate into the development of a training manual addressing physical preparation strategies for police operational activities, highlighting their practical educational value and direct applicability within law-enforcement training contexts.

TI INTERCULTURAL ATTITUDES AND PERCEPTIONS OF STUDENTS FROM THE UNITED
   STATES AND ROMANIA: COMPARATIVE STUDY AND INTEGRATION PERSPECTIVES
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE cross-cultural comparison; survey research; United States; Romania;
   cultural values.
AB This study investigates cultural attitudes and values across respondents from the United States and Romania. Drawing on cross-cultural psychology, modernization theory, and comparative survey methods, the research applies descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and Likert-scale analyses to identify areas of convergence and divergence between the two societies. The sample included 315 participants, of which 164 American and 151 Romanian students, attending master's programs in the fields of social work and psychology. In this research, we aimed to identify the main sets of values, principles, or attitudes acquired through university educational programs, which prepare graduates to practice their profession internationally. Results indicate both similarities in broad cultural orientations and significant differences in value priorities, with implications for theories of cultural persistence, modernization, and democratic development. The findings contribute to the growing literature on cross-national survey research and highlight methodological considerations for comparative studies.

TI STUDY CONCERNING THE PRESENCE OF ETHICAL VALUES IN THE CONDUCT OF

LA English
DT Article
DE ethical values; morality; education; moral behavior
ID MORAL VALUES
AB The purpose of ethical education is to develop critical thinking skills and cognitive capacities that allow individuals to identify the ethical dimensions of problems and to reflect on these problems by minimizing any negative effects. The school, as the main institution in the education of children, develops sustainable environments for character formation and ethical development. The study highlighted the quality of these environments in the sense that there are no significant differences between the ethical values promoted by students from rural areas compared to those from urban areas. Furthermore, no statistically significant differences were identified in the ethical values promoted by boys and girls, nor between students in the 7th and 8th grades. This finding suggests a degree of consistency in the educational environment experienced by the participants. Nevertheless, the results do not permit a clear distinction between the influence of the school environment and that of the family environment on the development of students' moral conduct. The role and strong influence of non-formal activities is underlined by the results of the study, in the sense that significant differences were observed in the level of ethical values between students who participated in extracurricular activities organized by the school and those who did not. Non-formal educational contexts that provide opportunities for reflection, dialogue and emotional involvement play a vital role in supporting the internalization of moral values. A preliminary analysis of ethical values among Romanian middle-school students using the EVA framework was previously reported by Albulescu et al. (2025). The present study extends these findings by examining gender and residential differences, the influence of extracurricular participation, psychometric characteristics of the instrument, and broader educational implications for moral development in adolescence.

TI EXPLORING ROMANIAN STUDENTS' PERSPECTIVES ON WOMEN'S RIGHTS, FREEDOMS
   AND GENDER RELATIONS IN ROMANIA AND AFGHANISTAN
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE women's rights and freedoms; gender; relations; Romania; Afghanistan;
   students' perception; factor analysis; comparative analysis
AB The purpose of ethical education is to develop critical thinking skills and cognitive capacities that a This study was carried out among students at Politehnica University of Timisoara, Romania, exploring their perceptions of women's rights and freedoms as well as gender relations both in Romania and Afghanistan, a country they primarily know through media representations. The main research objective was to gather insights into Romanian students' perceptions of gender issues within the distinct political and cultural contexts of the two countries. To facilitate this analysis, a questionnaire comprising 34 variables was administered, enabling a comparative examination of gender perceptions in Romania and Afghanistan. The findings revealed significant differences in how women's rights and freedoms are perceived in the two nations. In Romania, factor analysis identified four key dimensions: women's rights, violations of gender behavioral norms, sanctions for behavioural deviations, and punishment of women for adultery. In contrast, the analysis of Afghanistan revealed three main factors: women's rights, sanctions against men for behavioral deviations, and punishment of women. These results underscore the contrasting frameworks through which gender issues are understood in Romania and Afghanistan, reflecting deeper societal values and norms. Ultimately, this research highlights the critical role of context in shaping perceptions of gender rights, suggesting that students' views are influenced not only by their personal experiences but also by external narratives about different cultures.

TI TEACHING HEALTH SYSTEM EVIDENCE-BASED CURRICULA THROUGH COMPARATIVE
   POLICY ANALYSIS OF FRANCE AND SPAIN
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE teaching; economy; health; resilience; management; development
ID RESILIENCE
AB Health system resilience has emerged as a critical competency in health management education, yet pedagogical frameworks for teaching resilience through structured comparative analysis remain underdeveloped. This study addresses this gap by developing and demonstrating a replicable educational framework that integrates organizational resilience theory with comparative health policy analysis, specifically designed for graduate-level health management, public health, and public administration curricula. The study makes three distinct contributions to international health management education. Conceptually, it provides a unified analytical framework integrating macro-level policy analysis with meso-level institutional outcomes, enabling multi-scalar resilience teaching. Methodologically, it models rigorous secondary analysis research design accessible to graduate students in resource-constrained environments, supporting research literacy development. The pedagogical applications are immediate and concrete: the framework can be integrated directly into health systems governance courses, policy analysis modules, and crisis management curricula; the comparative findings provide structured case teaching material suitable for problem-based learning exercises; and the methodological transparency supports student-led comparative research projects. By explicitly connecting theoretical constructs, empirical evidence, and pedagogical implementation, the study advances evidence-informed curriculum development in health management education and provides a model for translating health systems research into teaching practice.

LA English
DT Article
DE educational consulting; master's students; selective educational
   components; didactic conditions; organization of the educational
   process; digitalization; model
AB The relevance of the topic is driven by the growing need to implement innovative approaches to the organization of the academic process that ensure high quality educational services and contribute to increasing the satisfaction of higher education seekers. The aim of the study is to develop a model of educational consulting and study the correlates of master's students' satisfaction with educational consulting. To solve the research tasks, a number of methods were used: analysis, synthesis, comparison, contrast; pedagogical modeling; questionnaires, interviews, surveys, observations; expert assessment methods; Spearman's correlation coefficient. TI TRANSLATION AND PSYCHOMETRIC VALIDATION OF THE PERMA-PROFILER IN A
   ROMANIAN STUDENT SAMPLE
SO REVISTA ROMANEASCA PENTRU EDUCATIE MULTIDIMENSIONALA
LA English
DT Article
DE positive psychology; well-being; PERMA-Profiler; Romanian version
ID ADAPTATION; GUIDELINES
AB The contemporary positive-psychology perspective departs from a purely deficit-based account of well-being. Instead of defining it by what is absent, namely distress, it characterizes wellbeing through several facets of functioning: the emotional, the psychological, and the social. In the Romanian context, research on psychological well-being has primarily relied on instruments measuring either subjective well-being or eudaimonic well-being. These instruments address important facets of well-being, but the model Martin Seligman proposed reaches further. Grouped under the label PERMA, its five elements are positive emotion, engagement, the quality of one's relationships, a sense of meaning, and a sense of accomplishment. The validated Romanian version of the PERMA-Profiler would facilitate research on flourishing, evaluation of well-being in clinical and non-clinical samples and would enable cross-cultural comparisons with international studies and intervention based on PERMA theoretical model. The present study aims at translating, culturally adapting and validating the PERMA-Profiler for use with Romanian populations. Although the evidence remains preliminary, it points to the Romanian version of the questionnaire as being both reliable and valid. These findings suggest that the PERMA-Profiler can be used as a multidimensional tool for assessing psychological flourishing in Romanian populations. The availability of a validated Romanian version may facilitate future research on well-being and enable cross-cultural comparisons within the field of positive psychology.

TI POLICIES, USE, AND TRAINING FOR THE INTEGRATION OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL
   INTELLIGENCE: A DOCUMENTARY ANALYSIS OF SPANISH PUBLIC UNIVERSITIES
SO SISYPHUSJOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence; generative artificial intelligence; public
   universities; content analysis
AB This research examines the institutional response of three Spanish public universities (University Jaume I, University of Val & egrave;ncia, and University of Lleida) to the emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). Drawing on a qualitative analysis of 26 institutional documents processed with ATLAS.ti, the study evaluates the regulatory frameworks and guidelines developed to govern its expansion within higher education. The findings reveal a significant reliance on European directives alongside still incipient internal regulations. The current institutional stance is predominantly preventive, emphasizing academic integrity, transparency, and best practices. Although the promotion of critical pedagogical uses and ethical literacy is evident, these institutions remain in a transitional phase toward more robust policy. Key challenges persist, notably the limited inclusion of technical staff in policy-making and the absence of standardized protocols to ensure long-term institutional sustainability.

TI REINTERPRETING DIGCOMPEDU IN HIGHER EDUCATION: ETHICAL CHALLENGES OF
   GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
SO SISYPHUSJOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE DigCompEdu; higher education; generative artificial intelligence;
   digital competence; ethics
AB The rapid expansion of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping higher education and challenging established conceptions of educators' digital competence. This article examines the European Framework for the Digital Competence of Educators (DigCompEdu) and its adaptation to higher education, analysing its capacity to address the ethical, pedagogical, and professional implications of GenAI. Adopting a competence-based analytical approach, the study critically explores how generative technologies intersect with the six DigCompEdu competence areas, with particular attention to data protection, human agency, academic integrity, equity, transparency, and sustainability. Drawing on international policy frameworks and scientific literature, the analysis highlights emerging gaps between existing digital competence models and the stochastic, opaque, and transformative nature of GenAI systems. The article argues for a human-centred and ethically grounded reinterpretation of DigCompEdu, capable of supporting responsible, inclusive, and accountable AI integration in higher education teaching and professional practice.

LA Spanish
DT Article
DE higher education; digital competence; artificial intelligence;
   validation; factor analysis
ID DIGITAL TEACHING COMPETENCE
AB The objectives of the study are to design and validate an instrument to assess perceptions and uses of Artificial Intelligence among teachers at a private university in Lima (Peru), as well as to analyse the results obtained. The research was carried out in two stages: an instrumental stage, aimed at evaluating the validity and reliability of the questionnaire, and a descriptive stage, aimed at analysing the results. A non-probabilistic convenience sample was used, with the participation of 385 university teachers from six academic areas. The results show that the instrument used achieves adequate levels of validity and reliability for measuring the proposed construct. AI is perceived positively by teachers; however, its integration into teaching practice is moderate. They highlight the need for a critical attitude towards AI-generated content, due to possible biases and inaccuracies, emphasizing reflective and responsible use in the educational field.

   COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF GUIDELINES IN GLOBAL ELITE UNIVERSITIES

LA English
DT Article
DE generative artificial intelligence; university governance; institutional
   policies; higher education; digital ethics
AB This study comparatively analyses the institutional guidelines of ten global elite universities, selected based on the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2025, regarding the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI). It adopts a qualitative, descriptive-analytical approach, grounded in documentary analysis of 87 institutional documents organised into four axes: teaching, student use, information security, and governance/ethics. TI ENGLISH DEVELOPMENT IN MOROCCAN HIGHER EDUCATION: CHALLENGES AND
   PROSPECTS
SO SISYPHUSJOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE english; natural evolution; linguistic conspiracy; higher education;
   post-colonialism
AB Moroccan higher education has witnessed various changes during the last decade. The shift from Licence-MasterDoctorat (LMD) to the Bachelor system through a more technical reform was not without effects on reshaping the linguistic situation and paving the way for English language to flourish at university. Using the lens of postcolonial theory and sociolinguistics, this empirical research relied on a mixed approach that combines quantitative and qualitative methods to explore the perceptions of students and professors on the status of English and the various macro and micro factors intervening with its development in Moroccan higher education. The implications drawn from this study revealed that strong internal socio-political factors led to the increasing positive tendency to adopt English in higher education and use it as a promising language for a better future career.

TI TEACHER TRAINING IN THE FACE OF THE CHALLENGES OF INCLUSION AND WORKING
   WITH GIFTED STUDENTS
SO SISYPHUSJOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE teacher training; giftedness; inclusive education; teaching work
AB Teachers have children with different needs in their classrooms and must address all of them in the teaching-learning process. In the case of giftedness, recognizing it and acting inclusively requires teachers to have extensive knowledge of the topic. In Portugal, there is little research on teacher training in giftedness, reinforcing the importance of understanding the challenges that the inclusion of gifted students in schools poses to teaching and the training of elementary school teachers. TI "The Text and Cultural Politics": Michael Apple's Enduring Contributions
   to Critical Education Research
SO AERA OPEN
LA English
DT Article
DE curriculum; educational policy; sociology; content analysis; Michael
   Apple; cultural politics; hegemony; relational analysis
AB This article examines Michael Apple's theoretical contributions to the field of education, with particular attention to his epistemological principle of relational analysis, his understanding of the State as a site of contestation, his use of Gramscian concepts of hegemony and common sense, and his analysis of educational policy as cultural politics. Drawing on Apple's foundational 1992 article, "The Text and Cultural Politics," this article argues that Apple's analytic tools remain indispensable for researchers seeking to understand how power operates in and through educational institutions. I demonstrate how Apple's framework enables researchers to move beyond economistic determinism while retaining a commitment to structural analysis and critique and how it opens space for understanding agency and counterhegemony in educational practice. The article concludes by pointing to the ongoing relevance of Apple's contributions for researchers engaged in critical educational policy studies today.

TI Understanding the Landscape of Rural Racial Achievement Gaps: Locale,
   Race, and Achievement Gaps
SO AERA OPEN
LA English
DT Article
DE achievement gap; equity; race; rural education; correlational analysis
ID SEGREGATION; POVERTY
AB Racial achievement gaps remain a significant concern in education research, yet far less is known about how these disparities manifest in rural communities. Using data from the Stanford Education Data Archive, this study examines White-Black and White-Hispanic achievement gaps in rural school districts, focusing on district-level predictors and variation across rural locale subcategories. Findings indicate that achievement gaps are associated with district demographics, socioeconomic status, and segregation, although relationships vary across racial groups and subjects. Higher proportions of English learners are consistently associated with wider gaps, while higher free or reduced-price lunch eligibility is associated with narrower gaps. Economic segregation is more consistently associated with gaps than racial segregation, particularly for White-Hispanic gaps. Results also reveal variation across rural locales, with Rural Fringe and Rural Distant districts exhibiting smaller gaps than Rural Remote districts. These findings highlight the importance of examining rural achievement gaps through both racial and geographic lenses.

TI The polyphonic symphony of pedagogy
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF ENGLISH EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE symphony ofpedagogy; professionalism; teacher agency; Garth Boomer
AB The Garth Boomer Address honours a forward thinking, insightful educator whose short time with us was marked by a fervent advocacy for the importance of respecting the professionalism and agency of teachers and placing our students at the centre of learning. Building on Boomer's (1982) argument that the complexity of English teaching is best understood through metaphor, I employ the metaphor of pedagogy as a polyphonic symphony in which melody, rhythm, and expressive qualities combine to create rich and engaging learning experiences. Boomer understood that art of fostering proficient language and literacy development is multidimensional and complex. He believed that teachers had the professionalism to make informed pedagogical choices responsive to the diverse needs of their students. He championed teacher and student autonomy. As teachers of English and literacy, we have the privilege of getting to know our students' stories, hearing their authentic voices, enriching their learning through the diverse and engaging world of literature and inspiring them to be creative and critical. We are the conductors of learning, and as such we will never reduce the art of teaching to one simple approach.

TI Representation matters: Diversity and inclusion in the senior Literature
   curriculum
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF ENGLISH EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Literature curriculum; English education; Text selection; Author
   demographics; Character demographics; Diversity representation
ID TEXT SELECTION; ENGLISH; CANON
AB This study examines trends in text selection for the Victorian Certificate of Education senior Literature course from 2001 to 2026, analysing 787 texts, comprising novels, plays, poetry anthologies, short story collections and other literature such as memoirs and essays. The research investigates the characteristics of texts, authors, and characters privileged in the curriculum, focusing on representation and diversity. Using a coding framework, the study quantifies trends in text types, publication dates, story settings, and author and character demographics. Key findings include gradual increases in authorship by women and people of colour. Character representation shows similar trends, with female protagonists increasing. These findings provide insights into the evolution of literary education and highlight areas for potential change in curriculum diversity. The study contributes to ongoing discussions about inclusivity and representation in literature education more broadly, offering valuable data for curriculum developers, educators, and policy-makers.

TI How the English curriculum in Aotearoa New Zealand was impoverished by
   knowledge-rich discourses
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF ENGLISH EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE English curriculum; reform; knowledge-rich; English paradigms; Te M &
   amacr;taiaho; Te Mataiaho
AB This article has been developed in the context of a tumultuous few years of political upheaval in Aotearoa, and unprecented 'reforms' to the education system both in character, scale and speed. It takes as its starting point Elizabeth Rata's opinion piece on a 'A knowledgke rich [sic] curriculum for New Zealand', posted on March 1, 2025 on the Open inquiry website, where she diagnoses the failings in the national English curriculum since the 1990s and offers her remedy. Central to the case I make here is the way in which subject English in all Anglophone settings regularly bears the brunt of misinformed accusations that the curriculum is failing students. The case I make is pragmatic: i.e., all English curriculums are describable as socially constructed models or paradigms, and the implementation of any model will have consequences for our students. At the start of my argument, I will indicate areas of sympathy with certain elements in Rata's argument, including her identification of a major shift in curriculum design that resulted from Lockwood Smith's Achievement Initiative in 1991. Like her, I would argue that the structure for English in Aotearoa subsequently led to what I would call an evacuation of content in English (not knowledge). However, this shift was not the product of a 'strange alliance of decolonisation and socialism' (Rata, 2025, para 5), but rather a global alliance of neoliberalism and narrowly standards-based assessment. Once these points of agreement and disagreement have been dealt with, I will offer an account of how the idea of a 'syllabus' disappeared from our country's educational conversation. I will conclude with a comparison of two recent curriculum developments, one commissioned by the former Labour government (2017-2023) and named Te Mataiaho: The English Curriculum refresh, the second developed in haste by a small cadre which conscripted and was conscripted by the current Coalition government's Minister of Education, Erica Stanford.

TI Authorial voice in adolescent multilingual writers: In-depth textual
   analysis
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF ENGLISH EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE authorial voice; writer's voice; author's voice; multilingual writers;
   academic writing; textual analysis; voice markers; high school writing;
   evaluative writing
ID CONSTRUCTION
AB Authorial voice plays a crucial role in academic writing, including high school evaluative genres; however, research on the nature of voice in adolescent writing and effective pedagogical strategies for teaching this concept is limited. This limitation is especially pressing for multicultural countries where increasingly diverse classrooms amplify the need for targeted support of multilingual students. To address this gap, this study investigated how multilingual students express their voice in an evaluative genre, text response, as they prepare for a high-stakes English examination in the final year of high school in Australia. Qualitative research methodology combining indepth textual analysis with talk-around-text interviews helped us examine the nature of textual voice via markers of authorial stance and reader engagement. The findings indicate the potential for multilingual students to strategically employ markers of stance to successfully support their evaluations in text responses. The study provides insights into potential avenues for empirical research, writing curriculum and instruction.

   education
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF ENGLISH EDUCATION

DT Article
DE Kate Lilley; poetry education; poetry; contemporary Australian poetry;
   teaching poetry
ID INTERVIEW
AB This article examines contemporary approaches to poetry education through an in-depth interview with Australian poet and academic Kate Lilley, whose distinguished career spans creative and scholarly domains. The interview investigates several critical dimensions of poetry pedagogy: the genre's position within contemporary cultural discourse; structural challenges within the Australian educational framework; and optimal instructional methodologies. TI 'The power of the question': How hip-hop pedagogy can reveal a discourse
   of questioning in Shakespeare education and Hamlet
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF ENGLISH EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Shakespeare; hip-hop pedagogy; Hamlet; questioning
ID CULTURE
AB Over 400 years after his death, Shakespeare and his works remain a significant part of modern society, the arts and education. However, Shakespeare has not always been received well by students, nor presented effectively by educators. This article and accompanying creative project, Who's there?, a hip-hop album based on the questions in Hamlet, explores how a hip-hop pedagogical approach could assist contemporary Australian educators to engage students in the works of Shakespeare and foster a discourse of questioning in the classroom. A close reading of one of the songs highlights the literary devices of narrative voice, intertextuality and questioning found not only in hip-hop songs but also in Shakespeare. This article proposes that a hip-hop pedagogical framework has the potential to improve student literacy and questioning skills, and student (and staff) engagement, and should therefore be considered in Australian Shakespeare education.

TI Health science clinical educators' self-reported knowledge and skills in
   supporting students-of-concern
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF WORK-INTEGRATED LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Clinical placement; health educators; clinical supervision; mental
   health; education
ID NURSING-STUDENTS; EXPERIENCES; QUALITY; WORK; PLACEMENT; NURSES
AB Work-integrated learning (WIL) provides students with essential practical experience, crucial to health professional education. Rising numbers of students-of-concern during clinical placements (placements) have increased the need for clinical educators (educators) to offer support. The definition of students-of-concern adopted in this paper are students who may be at risk of worsening mental health which interferes with their ability to be successful at university. This study investigated Australian health science educators' knowledge and skills in supporting students-of-concern on placement and identified resources to assist. Overall, 127 survey responses were collected. Less than half of the respondents felt supported by their workplace (n=44/126, 34.9%) and university partners (n=59/126, 46.9%). Enhanced educator training in supervising students-of-concern and ongoing institutional support is recommended to promote a proactive and preventative approach to student wellbeing.

TI The role of authentic assessment as a work-integrated learning model
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF WORK-INTEGRATED LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Work-integrated learning (WIL); employability; authentic assessment;
   multiplicity-WIL; professional social responsibility
ID HIGHER-EDUCATION; QUALITY; OUTCOMES
AB This case study presents the key outcomes, impacts and learnings gained from integrating a scaffolded authentic assessment (AA) WIL model, as part of a work-integrated learning (WIL) strategy within a Faculty at an Australian University. The series of three assessment interventions across three (minimum) core units functioned as a complement to existing WIL offerings. The model was designed to develop transferable skills with a focus on professional social responsibility within the context of the discipline being studied. Survey findings about the model reveal benefits for three key stakeholder groups: 1) for students by enhancing student employability learning for graduate success; 2) for faculty by strengthening the enculturation of scaffolded WIL interventions across the course; and 3) for employers by aligning employability skills and talent with evolving workforce needs. TI Evaluating placement quality: Rasch-based validation of the Clinical
   Placement Quality Survey - Student
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF WORK-INTEGRATED LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Work-integrated learning; student perceptions; placement experience;
   interprofessional; psychometric validation; health education
ID LEARNING-ENVIRONMENT; SUPERVISION; IMPACT; MODEL; NURSE
AB Health workforce readiness in part relies on the quality of placement experiences, but there are few validated tools to systematically capture students' perceptions. The Clinical Placement Quality Survey - Student (CPQS-S) was developed to capture health students' perceptions of placement quality, aligned with the Best Practice Clinical Learning Environment framework. This study evaluated the psychometric properties of the CPQS-S using Rasch analysis across multiple health disciplines, including clinical exercise physiology, exercise science, nutrition and dietetics, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, rehabilitation counselling, social work, and speech pathology. Responses from 933 students were analyzed in development and validation samples. The CPQS-S was found to measure a unidimensional construct, with items demonstrating strong fit and high separation reliability. These results support the CPQS-S as a reliable instrument for assessing student perceptions of placement experiences. Its validated structure highlights its potential to inform quality improvement initiatives across a range of traditional and broader work-integrated learning settings.

TI The student experience of paramedicine clinical facilitation in the
   out-of-hospital ambulance work-integrated learning placement: An
   exploratory study
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF WORK-INTEGRATED LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Student paramedic; clinical facilitation; work-integrated learning
ID NURSING-STUDENTS; MENTAL-HEALTH; PERCEPTIONS; PRECEPTOR
AB Work-integrated learning (WIL) placements are a vital part of healthcare education enabling students to integrate and consolidate theory to practice, demonstrate skills, socialize into the profession and create professional networks, develop their professional identity, and prepare for entering the workforce. The student paramedic out-of-hospital placement environment is uncontrolled and dynamic, often being high pressured and along with limited resources. In this exploratory study, the experiences of student paramedics receiving clinical facilitation were assessed. A self-reporting questionnaire was used to explore the student paramedic experiences of clinical facilitation in the out-of-hospital ambulance WIL placements. All participants identified advantages in having clinical facilitation in the out-of-hospital placement setting. Participants identified that clinical facilitators improved reflective practice for students, provided additional student support, and enhanced the learning opportunities for students. The key themes demonstrated the importance of adopting a clinical facilitator model for paramedic students undertaking out-of-hospital placements.

   learning; placement supervision
ID STUDENTS; EXPERIENCES; SATISFACTION
AB This article engages in a topical discussion regarding the training and development of staff who supervise students on placement (referred to as practice educators), with specific reference to social work education. TI Mapping ASEAN information and communication technology job trends to
   skills frameworks: A data-driven approach to aligning work-integrated
   learning
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF WORK-INTEGRATED LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE ASEAN ICT Skills; ICT education; job analysis; curriculum alignment;
   text mining
ID MARKET
AB This study investigates how real-time job analysis in Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) can be used to design work-integrated learning (WIL) programs and enhance the alignment between information and communication technology (ICT) education and labor market needs. Using text analysis techniques, 4,443 ICT employment positions were mapped to the ASEAN ICT Skills Standard to identify regional labor demand patterns. The results reveal both country-specific and shared trends. Software development, cloud computing, and cybersecurity are consistently in demand, whereas the Internet of Things (IoT) and social business reflect national economic orientations. Based on these findings, five strategies are proposed to improve WIL design: (1) role- and cross-role focus, (2) alignment with emerging technological trends, (3) diversification across job families, (4) identification of emerging skill clusters, and (5) responsiveness to regional-specific employment hubs. This research demonstrates a practical method for leveraging labor market data to inform curriculum planning and highlights the potential of ASEAN universities to develop WIL programs that provide students with more meaningful, industry-relevant learning experiences.

TI A comparison of the skills desired by businesses with those developed in
   experiential learning programs
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF WORK-INTEGRATED LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Experiential learning; theory of human relatedness; business programs;
   business skills
ID MANAGEMENT EDUCATION; SCHOOLS
AB This study critically examines the persistent global skills gap, particularly assessing the tension between corporate executive demands and higher education's primary responsibility, through a mixed-methods study conducted in the New York City region of the United States. AB Higher education institutions play a significant role in preparing graduates to tackle the complex challenges of the twenty-first century. TI Evaluating the resilience of work-integrated learning: A pharmacy co-op
   program case study
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF WORK-INTEGRATED LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Pharmacy; co-operative education; work-integrated learning; employment;
   resilience; Canada
ID COOPERATIVE EDUCATION; FUTURE
AB A descriptive analysis assessed how the University of Waterloo School of Pharmacy's co-op program adapted during significant changes in the healthcare environment. Work term data from 2017-2023 were analyzed, including new employer growth, breadth of sectors and geographical locations for co-op positions, and percentage of students who worked for their co-op employer post-graduation. During the timeframe, including the pandemic, the program recruited more jobs than students (2.3 jobs: student, range of 1.4 to 4.4 for an average class cohort size of 119 students per co-op term), averaging 17 new employers annually. Of jobs posted, 24.8% were outside community/hospital pharmacy settings. On average, 79.1% (74.2-84.7%) of students completed jobs outside the local urban area of Waterloo, Ontario, and 53% of alumni reported accepting a paid job with their co-op employer within five years post-graduation. By continuously growing sector engagement to align with changes in core and emerging healthcare settings, the co-op program demonstrated resilience by reliably providing students with relevant work settings.

TI The CHIRO-Force peer-assisted learning program for manual therapy
   education
SO JOURNAL OF CHIROPRACTIC EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Chiropractic; Musculoskeletal manipulations; Mentoring; Feedback;
   Education
ID SPINAL MANIPULATION; PERFORMANCE
AB Objective: Peer mentoring is increasingly valued in healthcare education for developing professional and clinical competencies. In the chiropractic program at our university, Force-Sensing Table Technology (FSTT (R)) was first integrated to enhance manual therapy training. After this, the CHIRO-Force Peer-Assisted Learning (PAL) program was launched as a collaborative learning process to further train students in practical skills related to chiropractic manual therapies. This paper introduces the program and reports findings from its first year. Methods: The CHIRO-Force program was structured and evaluated using the PAL learning framework. After pilot funding approval, 2 fourth-year students were selected as mentors. Then, they and 2 faculty members completed intensive training from the developers of the FSTT (R) technology. Mentors then designed session protocols and organized a booking system. Mentees were invited to complete a short questionnaire after each session and a comprehensive one at the end of the pilot year. The program launched in September 2023 and the pilot year ended in April 2024. Results: Mentors created 5 distinct session protocols and each dedicated about 5 hours weekly to mentoring. From September to April, more than 100 sessions were provided, involving over 100 students. Group mentoring was also integrated into clinical internships. Feedback was highly positive, with 97% of sessions rated as "highly appreciated". Conclusion: The CHIRO-Force PAL program shows promise in supporting students' practice of spinal manipulative therapy outside class. Future steps include assessing its impact on clinical competency and self-efficacy.

TI Psychometric Evaluation of Forensic Medicine Multiple-Choice Questions:
   An Item Analysis From a Nepali Medical College
SO JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND CURRICULAR DEVELOPMENT
LA English
DT Article
DE medical education; item analysis; multiple-choice questions; forensic
   medicine; assessment; Nepal
ID IMPACT
AB Background Multiple-choice questions (MCQs) are test items that are essential to assess the competency of medical students in forensic medicine. However, the psychometric quality of these test items in Nepali medical colleges remains largely unexplored. This study evaluated the difficulty index, discrimination index, and distractor effectiveness of forensic medicine MCQs to identify areas requiring improvement.Methods This cross-sectional study evaluated 30 MCQs from the end-of-semester forensic medicine examination which was administered to 100 third-year medical students. The item difficulty, the discrimination index (via Kelley's 27% method), and performance of the distractor were calculated for each question.Results The students showed high performance, with a mean score of 23.25 +/- 3.61 out of 30. Difficulty analysis showed that majority of the items (60%) fell within an acceptable difficulty range (70-90% correct), while 16.7% were very easy and 6.6% were difficult. Discrimination was good in 43.3% of the items, moderate in 23.3%, and poor in 33.3%. Distractor analysis identified non-functional distractors in a large proportion of items, including nine items (30%) with at least one zero-response option. Overall, 44 of 90 distractors (48.9%) across all items were non-functional. A statistically significant negative correlation was found between item difficulty and discrimination index (rho = -0.4265, p = 0.019); items of moderate difficulty (50-69% correct) showed the highest mean discrimination, with both moderate- and acceptable-difficulty items outperforming items at the extremes of difficulty.Conclusions The examination revealed adequate student performance; however, item quality analysis demonstrated the need for improvement, with approximately one-third of the items failing to meet the desired standard and therefore requiring revision due to poor discrimination or non-functional distractors. Structured faculty training in item-writing principles and regular psychometric evaluation may help improve assessment quality in Nepali medical education.

TI A Three-Year Multi-Faculty Evaluation of 16 SI-PASS Schemes: Attendance
   Thresholds, Performance Gains, and Standardized Metrics
SO JOURNAL OF PEER LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
ID SUPPLEMENTAL INSTRUCTION; PEER; PROGRAM; UNIVERSITY; EDUCATION
AB The study scrutinizes 16 iterations of a regular SI-PASS program across four faculties in a Belgian university over a three-year span. The large dataset enables inter-year and inter-faculty comparisons, illuminating the program's convergent and varying traits. Throughout the study period, 78.32% of the targeted audience attended at least one session. Participants' reported motives for attending primarily relate to improved understanding of course material and enhanced social integration. A quasi-experimental design exhibits a significant improvement of the mark at the exam in 10 instances. This performance gain is conditioned by five, six, seven, or eight participations depending on the faculty and year concerned. The results are intentionally reported according to standard indicators defined at the European level for SI-PASS and supplemented with locally developed metrics found useful to support program monitoring and institutional accountability. The paper concludes on a call to SI-PASS hosts to share similarly precise and standardized descriptors to uplift international comparability and collective learning.

AB In South Africa, research on reading in schools on a national scale promotes a deficit view that learners cannot read for meaning. DT Article
DE digital storytelling; group work; individual work; speaking skills;
   anxiety level
ID ENGLISH
AB This study aimed to measure the effect of digital storytelling (DST) on speaking performance, foreign language anxiety, and speaking anxiety in an English-learning environment. Forty-eight (48) Omani students of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) with intermediate English proficiency levels were randomly and equally assigned to one control and two experimental groups. Experimental Group A engaged in designing DST projects in groups, Experimental Group B created the DST projects individually, and the Control group performed some paper-based short story reviews. In addition, the FLCAS results showed that the two experimental groups displayed less language learning anxiety in the learning process, and Experimental Group A's anxiety was markedly lower than that of the other groups. The analysis of SLSAS revealed that Experimental Group A showed lower anxiety than Group B in speaking skills. The results of the study are helpful for the teachers and students.

ID COMPREHENSION; TEXT
AB As a critical component of literacy, strong reading skills open doors for personal advancement and gainful employment. Yet, despite South Africa moving to a new democratic dispensation almost three decades ago, little progress has been made to remedy literacy problems in schools. The key to eradicating this dilemma lies largely with school language and literacy teachers. Teachers should have robust reading attitudes and habits to serve as good role models for learners. This exploratory study reports the reading attitudes and habits of 444 Foundation and Intermediate Phase pre-service teachers training to teach English. The findings have implications for teacher training and language instruction in disrupting the cycle of literacy challenges and replacing it with reading confidence and a love of literature and learning.

TI ENGLISH AS A SECOND LANGUAGE TEACHERS' ATTITUDES TOWARDS THE E-SOURCING
   OF LITERARY MATERIALS FOR ESL TEACHING
SO PER LINGUAM-A JOURNAL OF LANGUAGE LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE attitudes; coerced willingness; communicative competence; English second
   language; literary materials; literature; mobile devices; reading
   culture; technology; TPACK
ID USER ACCEPTANCE; INFORMATION; TECHNOLOGY
AB There is an ever-increasing demand for ESL teachers to focus on literature to teach language and improve learners' English proficiency. However, in Eswatini, literature is not prioritised at the primary school level and there are limited resources for ESL teachers eager to teach ESL using literary materials. While mobile devices may be a solution for e-sourcing such materials, there is limited research on whether ESL teachers have adopted mobile devices for this practice. This interpretivist qualitative case study investigated the attitudinal beliefs of nine ESL teachers on adopting this practice. Data were generated through observations, interviews and document analysis. Through the lens ofMishra and Koehler's technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK), Venkatesh et al.'s unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT), Davis's technology acceptance model (TAM), and Vygotsky's Socio-cultural theory (SCT) frameworks, we thematically analysed and interpreted the generated data. Findings revealed that even though ESL teachers had positive attitudinal beliefs about e-sourcing literary materials, they did not source them owing to deficiencies in the learners' reading culture, dogmatism, coerced willingness, and confidence deficiency in technological, pedagogical and content knowledge (TPACK). This study recommends employing TPACK and transformational leadership training, English curriculum review, and providing schools with Wi-Fi facilities.

TI Are doctors' soft skills adequately supported by medical curricula? A
   study on medical schools in Turkiye.
SO SPANISH JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Soft Skills; medical education; medical curriculum; curriculum analysis
ID PHYSICIAN COMMUNICATION; PATIENT COMMUNICATION; EMPATHY; EDUCATION;
   STUDENTS
AB This study aims to investigate the extent to which soft skills, which are an important element that complements the technical skills of physicians, are included in the curricula of medical schools in Turkiye. The websites of all medical schools in Turkiye were accessed and the curricula of the 20232024 academic year were examined using the content analysis method. Based on the categories of soft skills identified by the Malaysian Ministry of Higher Education, it was analyzed whether these courses were included in the curricula and in which categories and medical education periods they were offered. It was found that all the medical schools under study had elective or compulsory soft skills courses. However, 12.3% of universities did not include a compulsory soft skills course in their curriculum. While 83% of the universities concentrated soft skills courses exclusively in the first three years of medical education, only 2.3% of medical schools spread these courses over the entire education period, including the last three years. Examining the distribution of courses by category revealed that courses in the field of 'Communication' were the most common, followed by courses in the categories of 'Ethics' and 'Lifelong Learning and Information Technologies'. Courses in the categories 'Critical Thinking and Problem Solving', 'Leadership' and 'Teamwork' were found to be significantly underrepresented. It is recommended to design the curricula of medical faculties to include all categories of soft skills and to spread them programmatically throughout the educational process.

   Qualitative Exploration of Student Engagement, Perceived Educational
   Implications, and Ethical Considerations
SO ADVANCES IN MEDICAL EDUCATION AND PRACTICE
LA English
DT Article
DE generative artificial intelligence; health informatics students;
   artificial intelligence literacy; educational technology; academic
   integrity; qualitative research; Saudi Arabia
ID UNIVERSITY; AI
AB Background: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in higher education and health sciences education. However, limited qualitative evidence has examined how undergraduate Health Informatics (HI) students in Saudi Arabia engage with GenAI and interpret its educational, cognitive, ethical, and institutional implications. Aim: This study aimed to explore HI students' perceptions and self-reported experiences of GenAI use within academic learning Methods: A qualitative study informed by an interpretivist approach and reflexive thematic analysis was conducted across six Saudi public universities offering undergraduate HI programmes. Thirty undergraduate HI students with prior academic experience using GenAI were purposively recruited. Semi-structured interviews were conducted over a two-month period in 2026 using face-to-face and online modalities. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, anonymized, and analyzed iteratively using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis approach with support from ATLAS.ti software. Results: Three themes were identified: engagement with GenAI; perceived benefits and limitations; and ethical and institutional considerations. Participants reported using GenAI to summarize materials, understand complex concepts, organize academic tasks, and support assignments. They perceived GenAI as useful for efficiency and comprehension but also described concerns about over-reliance, reduced independent learning, passive acceptance of outputs, plagiarism, lack of source transparency, and unclear institutional policies. Conclusion: Undergraduate HI students in Saudi Arabia perceived GenAI as a useful academic support tool, while also identifying cognitive, ethical, and institutional challenges. These exploratory findings reflect perceptions and self-reported experiences rather than objectively measured educational outcomes. Structured AI literacy, clear institutional guidance, and responsible curriculum integration are needed in HI education.

TI Factors Associated with Perceived Continuing Medical Education Necessity
   Among General Practitioners in Southeast Henan, China
SO ADVANCES IN MEDICAL EDUCATION AND PRACTICE
LA English
DT Article
DE general practitioners; continuing medical education; influencing
   factors; primary care
AB Background: Continuing medical education (CME) is crucial for maintaining the competency of general practitioners (GPs). Understanding factors associated with GPs' perceived necessity of CME is essential for optimizing training programs, especially in resource-constrained regions. This study aimed to identify factors associated with GPs' perceived necessity of CME in Southeast Henan, China. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among GPs in Zhoukou City, Southeast Henan, from August to September 2024. Data were collected via an online questionnaire. The primary outcome was the perceived necessity of CME (binary: yes/no). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were employed to identify factors associated with this outcome. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to explore pathways linking CME policy cognition, self-efficacy, attitude towards CME, and perceived necessity. Results: Among 5537 eligible registered GPs, 2,480 valid responses were obtained (response rate, 44.8%). Overall, 35.6% perceived CME as necessary, whereas 89.6% had participated in CME during the previous three years. In the multivariable model, understanding the linkage between CME credits and career advancement showed the strongest positive association with perceived CME necessity (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=3.74, 95% CI: 2.97-4.72). Organizational support (aOR=1.76), high self-directed learning ability (aOR=1.60), absence of anxiety (aOR=1.37), and more than 30 years of practice experience (aOR=1.58) were also positively associated with perceived CME necessity. Conclusion: The perceived necessity of CME among GPs was associated with policy awareness, organizational support, psychological factors, and professional experience. These findings may inform policy transparency, organizational support, and tiered CME curricula that address the needs of GPs with different competency levels.

TI Interdisciplinary Development of 3D-Printed Anatomical Models for Human
   Gross Anatomy Education
SO ADVANCES IN MEDICAL EDUCATION AND PRACTICE
LA English
DT Article
DE 3D printing; anatomy education; anatomical models; additive
   manufacturing; human gross anatomy; educational evaluation
ID MEDICAL-STUDENTS; 3D; SCIENCES; CORE
AB Purpose: To describe the interdisciplinary development of two 3D-printed anatomical models-a trigeminal nerve model and a lower airway model-and to explore their perceived usefulness in the teaching of human gross anatomy. This study presents an interdisciplinary experience of design, fabrication, and initial educational evaluation of 3D-printed anatomical models developed to support anatomy teaching in an institutional context with limited access to cadaveric material. Methods: This methodological and educational study was conducted in three phases. First, teaching and learning needs in human gross anatomy were identified through classroom-based inquiry and faculty input. The preliminary assessment indicates positive user perception and supports their use as complementary teaching tools. Future studies should include controlled comparisons and objective learning outcomes to assess their educational impact more robustly.

TI BRIDGES BETWEEN NEUROSCIENCE AND TEACHING PRACTICE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
   OF NEURODIDACTIC STRATEGIES
SO AULA DE ENCUENTRO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Neurodidactics; neuroeducation; meaningful learning; emotional
   regulation; teaching practices
AB Advances in neuroscience have provided a deeper understanding of the cognitive, emotional, and social processes involved in learning, although their pedagogical application remains limited and hindered by neuromyths. This systematic review analysed the effectiveness of neurodidactic strategies within formal educational contexts. Searches were conducted across Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and Academic Search Ultimate for empirical studies published between 2015 and 2025, assessing methodological quality according to PRISMA 2020 and EPHPP guidelines. Out of 95 identified records, 10 met inclusion criteria. Results indicated that strategies such as active learning, multisensory teaching, emotional support, and teacher training in neuroscience improved academic performance, emotional self-regulation, intrinsic motivation, and student satisfaction. It is concluded that neurodidactic strategies constitute an effective resource for integrating brain knowledge into inclusive and engaging pedagogical practices, highlighting the need for specialized teacher training and longitudinal studies to evaluate long-term impact.

TI The effect of rapid automatized naming ability in elementary school on
   reading comprehension: the mediating role of sustained attention
SO EGITIM VE BILIM-EDUCATION AND SCIENCE
LA English
DT Article
DE Rapid automatized naming; Reading comprehension; Sustained attention;
   Curriculum-based assessment
ID WORKING-MEMORY; PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS; RAN; PREDICTORS; FLUENCY; SPEED;
   COMPONENTS; MECHANISM
AB The purpose of this study is to test the effect of sustained attention's mediating role on the impact of rapid automatized naming ability on reading comprehension. The participants in the study consisted of 56 third-grade elementary school students. Of the participants, 53.57% were female (n=30) and 46.43% were male (n=26). The age range of the students, who are from the same school and similar socioeconomic backgrounds, varies between 8.24 and 8.77 (x=8.41, SD= 0.19). The native language of all students participating in the study is Turkish. A structural equation model was used to analyze the data obtained in the study. SPSS 24 was used for the necessary analyses in the study, namely correlation and Sobel z-test, while SmartPLS 4 was used for the mediation test and the equality model. The results of the study show that there is a significant relationship between the sub-dimensions of rapid automatized naming (object, color, letter), reading comprehension, and sustained attention, while there is no significant relationship between reading comprehension and number naming. Another result of the study is that rapid automatized naming has a direct (beta=-.19, t=3.22, p<.05) and indirect (beta=-.18) effect on reading comprehension. The direct relationship between rapid automatized naming and reading comprehension was found to be significant when the mediating variable was not included in the model. However, when the mediating variable of sustained attention was added to the model, this direct effect became insignificant. Therefore, it was concluded that sustained attention complately mediated this effect.

TI The effect of the nature of science activities on 5th-grade students'
   scientific process skills
SO EGITIM VE BILIM-EDUCATION AND SCIENCE
LA English
DT Article
DE Science education; Science Process Skills (SPS); Nature of Science
   (NOS); 5th-grade students
ID TEACHING NATURE; INSTRUCTION; EDUCATION; EXPLICIT; VIEWS
AB The Nature of Science (NOS) and Scientific Process Skills (SPS) are central components of science education, as they play a crucial role in fostering students' scientific reasoning, inquiry competence, and understanding of how scientific knowledge is constructed. This study aimed to investigate the effects of NOS-based activities implemented in science classes on the development of fifth-grade students' scientific process skills. The research employed a single-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design with fifth-grade students from a public school in Denizli/Beya & gbreve;a & ccedil;, T & uuml;rkiye, over an eight-week period. The NOS activities were designed to introduce students to scientific processes, promote scientific thinking, and facilitate the integration of science into everyday life. Data were collected using the Basic Skills Scale and the Scientific Process Skills Evaluation Form (SPSEF). The analysis of the Basic Skills Scale indicated a significant improvement in posttest scores compared to pretest levels. In addition, the analysis of activity-based data collected through the SPSEF revealed improvements in higher-order skills, including problem identification, variable recognition, hypothesis formulation, experimental design, and data interpretation. These findings suggest that integrating explicit-reflective NOS activities into science instruction can effectively support the development of both basic and emerging higher-order scientific process skills at early grade levels, while also enhancing students' understanding of the epistemic nature of scientific knowledge.

TI Evaluating the effectiveness of reading comprehension-based instruction
   supported by flipped learning model in the 7th grade science course
SO EGITIM VE BILIM-EDUCATION AND SCIENCE
LA English
DT Article
DE Science course; Teaching science; Reading comprehension; Flipped
   learning; Instructional design
ID STRATEGY INSTRUCTION; KNOWLEDGE; ABILITY; SKILLS; MOTIVATION; TEXTS
AB Reading comprehension is a crucial skill that underpins the understanding of scientific concepts and processes, facilitates the integration of conceptual knowledge with analytical thinking, and thereby enhances scientific literacy. In this context, the flipped learning model allows students to explore essential concepts at home through digital resources, thus freeing classroom time for targeted interventions. In this study, it was aimed to evaluate the effect of reading comprehension-based science instruction, supported by a flipped learning model, on the learning and reading comprehension skills of 7th-grade students during the 2022-2023 academic year in a boys-only public middle school in Istanbul. By employing an embedded mixed design, the effectiveness of reading comprehension-based instruction was evaluated during and after the implementation stage by conducting an experimental design and collecting both qualitative and quantitative data. In total, 67 students participated. In the experimental groups, students learned basic concepts at home through assignments from the Education Science Network before class, while in-class activities focused on applying reading comprehension skills to scientific content. Data were gathered through various measurement tools, including a reading comprehension skills scale, an achievement test, teacher reflection notes, and semi-structured interviews. The findings showed that students significantly showed improvement in their reading comprehension and science performance. Students stated that they achieved better understanding and learning through reading strategies that they could apply in other courses. In addition, the instruction contributed to their social-emotional development, including selfawareness, social skills and academic motivation.
